title: AI Product Engineer
description:
Das ist kein gewöhnlicher Job. Wir arbeiten an dem, was unsere Gesellschaft zukunftsfähig macht: Bildung. Dafür bauen wir paddy, das Agentic Operating System für Teaching & Learning.

Unsere Mission ist es, Lehrkräfte zu entlasten, Lernergebnisse zu verbessern und die Unterrichtsqualität zu steigern.

Tausende Lehrkräfte und hunderttausende Lernende nutzen paddy bereits. Mit starken Investoren im Rücken wachsen wir schnell. Unsere Ambition ist es, den europäischen AI-Player für Bildung zu bauen.

Als AI Product Engineer übernimmst du Probleme unserer Nutzer End-to-End: vom Verständnis des Problems über Architektur, Backend und Frontend bis zum Deployment. Du prüfst, ob die Lösung im Klassenzimmer wirklich funktioniert. Dein Schwerpunkt liegt auf AI Engineering: Du baust die agentischen Systeme, die paddy ausmachen, und bringst sie zuverlässig, schnell und bezahlbar in Production.

Aufgaben

  • Agentische Systeme bauen: Du entwickelst die Agent-Architektur von paddy weiter.
  • KI in Production betreiben: Mit Evals, Guardrails und AI Observability sorgst du dafür, dass Qualität, Kosten und Latenz unserer KI-Features kein Zufall sind.
  • End-to-End shippen: Du baust Features vom Verständnis des Problems bis zur fertigen Lösung und verantwortest, wie sie im Schulalltag funktionieren.
  • Produktnah arbeiten: Du sprichst mit Lehrkräften, erkennst echte Bedarfe und triffst mit Product und Design Entscheidungen, statt auf Tickets zu warten.
  • Engineering-Bar heben: Testing, Monitoring und saubere Architektur geben dir Geschwindigkeit. Du erkennst Risiken früh und steuerst technische Schulden bewusst.

Qualifikation

  • Product-Engineering-Erfahrung: Mindestens drei Jahre Erfahrung mit digitalen Produkten und echten Nutzer.
  • AI-Engineering-Know-how: Du hast LLM-Features oder agentische Systeme gebaut und in Production betrieben. Du verstehst Modellfehler, RAG, Evals und Vektor-Datenbanken. ML Research ist nicht erforderlich.
  • Technisches Fundament: Du bist sicher in API-Design, Datenmodellen und der Entwicklung über Backend und Frontend hinweg.
  • Ownership und Urteilskraft: Du kommst mit offenen Problemen klar, findest einfache Lösungen für komplexe Fragen und baust Systeme, die im Schulalltag funktionieren.
  • AI-native Arbeitsweise: Du nutzt Coding Agents und moderne AI-Tools selbstverständlich, um deinen Output zu vervielfachen.
  • Sprachen: Fließend Deutsch und sehr gutes Englisch.

Unser Tech Stack

  • Full-stack TypeScript: Next.js, Drizzle, Postgres
  • Web: Next.js, Tailwind, Zod
  • Mobile: React Native, Expo, EAS, React Query
  • AI: Vercel AI SDK, promptfoo, LiteLLM, Arize Phoenix, pgVector
  • Infra: DigitalOcean, Scaleway, Open Telekom Cloud, Azure

Benefits

  • Sichtbaren Impact: Du arbeitest am wichtigsten Zukunftsthema unserer Gesellschaft, der Bildung.
  • 70.000 bis 100.000 € Bruttojahresgehalt, abhängig von deiner Erfahrung, plus Equity (VSOP).
  • 100 % Remote-Arbeit. Wenn du lieber ins Büro kommst, steht dir unser modernes Office in Bielefeld offen.
  • Großen Gestaltungsspielraum und Ownership sowie direkte Zusammenarbeit mit den Foundern und einem starken Product- und Engineering-Team.
  • Ein hohes Budget, solange der Nutzen stimmt.
  • Zeit und Unterstützung für deine Entwicklung, mit Fortbildungsbudget, Coaching und klaren Entwicklungsperspektiven.
  • 30 Urlaubstage und 50 € monatlichen steuerfreien Sachbezug.
  • Regelmäßige Team-Events und Offsites.
  • Starkes Backing durch erfahrene Investoren und Mentoren.

Unser Bewerbungsprozess

Wenn die Kalender passen, können wir den gesamten Prozess innerhalb von fünf Tagen abschließen.

  1. Kennenlernen, Tag 1: Im ersten Gespräch schauen wir, ob es für beide Seiten passt. Wenn ja, vereinbaren wir direkt deinen Probetag.
  2. Probetag mit Case Study, Tag 4: Du arbeitest mit uns an einer echten Aufgabe und stellst anschließend dein Ergebnis vor.
  3. Gespräch mit unserem CEO, Tag 4: Das Gespräch findet am Abend deines Probetags statt.
  4. Teamgespräch, Tag 5: Du lernst die Engineers kennen, mit denen du arbeiten wirst.
  5. Entscheidung, Tag 5: Nach dem Teamgespräch geben wir dir unsere finale Rückmeldung.

Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen. Erzähl uns, welche Probleme du gelöst, welche Entscheidungen du getroffen und welche Systeme du in Produktion gebracht hast.

title: Staff Quality Engineer - Mobile
description:
About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

  • Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

  • Profitable since 2017

  • Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

  • Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role

At Lendable we already have a number of profitable, award winning credit products. They have a good automated quality story. However, as our customer base has grown into the millions we need to keep evolving to keep the quality bar high. Advances in AI engineering also have enabled us to ship faster, but we need to ensure we are not regressing on our quality metrics.

Our mobile app, Zable, is how most of our customers experience all of our products in one centralised space. It's written in React Native and TypeScript with a Kotlin backend, shipped to iOS and Android from a single codebase. We are now looking to level up the quality engineering so that we can raise release cadence without losing sleep over regressions.

This is an automation-first role. You'll spend most of your time writing code - test frameworks, CI tooling, helpers, rather than executing test scripts by hand. You'll work alongside software engineers, product, and design, setting direction.

You'll also be working at the frontier of AI-assisted quality, using LLMs and AI tooling to speed up test authoring, triage failures, and surface coverage gaps, while applying the engineering judgement to keep tests trustworthy.

 
 

What you'll be doing

Own the mobile test strategy:

  • Define and evolve a pragmatic test pyramid for React Native - deciding where E2E is worth the weight and where logic belongs in faster layers (Jest, React Testing Library, component tests).

  • Make deliberate calls about coverage, reliability, and speed trade-offs across the app.

  • Set the bar for what "ready to ship" looks like on mobile, and hold the line on it.

Enable teams to keep the quality bar high

  • Rotating around different product teams for short periods to level up quality

  • Define and evolve the pragmatic test pyramid for our products - deciding where E2E is worth the weight and where testing belongs in faster layers (unit and component tests)

  • Make deliberate calls about coverage, reliability, and speed trade-offs across our products

  • Devise and set up performance benchmarks to ensure critical parts of our systems don't regress

 

Bring AI testing into the SDLC

  • Speed up our SDLC by building agents that exploratory test changes and catch issues before they get to production

  • Use AI tools day-to-day to accelerate test authoring, cluster failures, surface coverage insights, and propose fixes

  • Decide where AI adds leverage and where a human eye is needed. A test suite that looks comprehensive but isn't trustworthy is worse than a smaller one we rely on

Build reliable E2E automation

  • Discover gaps in testing and help teams build comprehensive suites

  • Get test environments and data fixtures to a level where they are easy to use and reliable

  • Drive flakiness down and time-to-diagnosis down. We treat a flaky test the same way we treat a broken test, and we expect root-cause work rather than retry-until-green

Prevent defects, not just catch them

  • Partner with product and engineering on shift-left quality: join specs early, push back on ambiguous acceptance criteria, and surface risk before code is written

  • Close the loop on production issues using our observability stack (Datadog, Sentry, Grafana) - tying test coverage back to real customer impact

  • Ensure teams have Service Level Objectives set up and are achieving them

  • Run targeted exploratory testing on high-risk releases when it's the right call

     

What we're looking for

Essential

  • Hands-on experience with Maestro or Detox.

  • 5+ years in quality engineering or test automation, with a track record of keeping automated suites stable rather than letting them rot into a graveyard of quarantined tests

  • Experience working in a scaled engineering environment with multiple teams pulling in different directions and priorities, and know how to navigate that to drive quality improvements across them

  • Hands-on coding experience of writing test code, frameworks, CI pipelines and other helper scripts. You know what a good test codebase looks like and you constantly improve it

  • API and contract testing experience, with a point of view on test data and environment strategy

  • Have set up and used Service Level Objectives to define a contract of system reliability with stakeholders, and driven measurable improvements against them

  • Native AI-assisted working style. You can describe projects where AI meaningfully changed how you worked - test authoring, failure triage, coverage analysis - and where you decided it wasn't the right tool

  • Coaching other disciplines in quality. You evangelise quality practices and get others on board to solve quality problems together

  • Experience shaping CI/CD pipelines for test reliability (GitHub Actions or similar), including flakiness reduction, parallelisation, artefact management, and runtime control

  • Proactive, low-ego, and clear communicator, able to chase things down when blocked

  • Able to operate independently and drive improvements end-to-end (frameworks, CI, test data, reporting)

  • Can point to 3-4 projects where you moved the needle on quality - for example improving SLO coverage or reducing incident rate - and can speak to the measurable impact of each

Nice to have

  • Hands-on experience testing React Native apps.

  • Mobile performance and reliability work (crash reporting, startup time, memory and battery awareness).

  • API and contract testing experience, with a point of view on test data and environment strategy.

     

Our tech stack

Mobile: TypeScript, React Native, Expo, EAS, GraphQL, Relay, Jest, React Testing Library, Maestro.

Backend: Kotlin, PHP 8 (Symfony), AWS, Postgres, RabbitMQ, Docker, Kubernetes.

Tooling and observability: GitHub, GitHub Actions, Jira, Confluence, Datadog, Sentry, Grafana.

Why join?

  • See your work matter: Our products are used by millions of customers - the quality bar you help set has a direct line to customer trust and company revenue

  • High impact: You'll decide where and how to engage across teams to move quality forward, working hands-on rather than through process layers

  • Work at the frontier of AI: AI tooling for quality is moving fast. You'll be one of the people deciding how we apply it - what's useful, what isn't, and where to keep humans in the loop

  • An organisation that ships: No layers, no theatre, fast decisions

     

Interview process

  • Quick call with a Recruiter

  • 15 minute cognitive test

  • Hiring manager interview (30 minutes)

  • Technical interview (60 minutes)

  • Culture interview (60 minutes)

Life at Lendable

  • Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

  • Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover

  • Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans

  • Employee referral programme: earn a competitive bonus when you refer successful new team members

  • Office meals & snacks: enjoy a fully stocked kitchen, plus complimentary lunches prepared by in-house chefs on in-office days at select locations

  • Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations

Please note: The availability and details of specific benefits vary by location and role. For more information, please speak to your Talent Partner.

Check out our blog!

title: Product Engineer
description:
The Context

Banks still run their most critical, regulated work by hand; reading letters and emails, re-keying data between systems, chasing down missing info. It's the kind of work that's too important to get wrong and too tedious for anyone to want to do.

Porters fixes this. Our AI agents run these regulated processes end to end, with the audit trails and security banks actually require, so the work moves at the speed customers expect instead of the speed a backlog allows.

We're just over a year old and already live with real customers, growing the product quickly, and were named Fintech of the Year 2026. The goal is to build the operating system for autonomous banking. We're backed by Earlybird, one of Europe's oldest venture firms, and Seedcamp, who wrote first checks into Revolut, Wise, and UiPath.

The Mission

You'll own features in their entirety. Self-standing or with guidance of founders and fellow engineers, you turn a clear problem statement into a strong design and build, test, and ship new features that directly enable our customers. You integrate features across our layered stack, from the API to the data plane, and carry them all the way to production.

This job is in person in Zurich, or remote in Barcelona or Berlin.

Your responsibilities

  • Ship features end-to-end: Deliver complete vertical slices across the stack, from the API layer to the data model, carried through to running in production.

  • Grow what the platform does for banks: Build the services Porters performs for banks: Extend the capabilities of our agentic platform such as case handling, customer matching, AI tool integrations, data enrichment, or keeping humans in the loop.

  • Deliver features that hold together as a system: Design endpoints, contracts, and interfaces that work together, ensuring features integrate cleanly towards one bigger outcome.

  • Ensure your work is reliable: Own design, development, tests, and deployment, so what reaches production is proven to work.

  • Wow our customers: You solve for the customer's actual problem, not just the request and measure success by customer outcomes. What would it take for the customer to say “Porters, made my day”.

Your profile

  • Experience: Around 4 years of professional software engineering, with a track record of shipping in fast-paced, ambiguous environments. Regulated industry and/or VC-backed startup experiences are a plus.

  • Product thinking: You naturally understand why you’re building something, not just focusing on how to build.

  • Quality focus & individual problem solving: Given a clear problem, you reliably produce a clean algorithm, a sensible data model, a well-structured service. You treat tests and observability as part of the feature, and right-size rigor to risk. You are comfortable in a regulated fintech environment where precision matters.

  • Technical proficiency: Proficiency in Python is mandatory, along with REST API development, an ORM, and relational databases.

  • AI-native: You've worked with, or are eager to work with, LLM/agentic tooling, and understand how to bound probabilistic output with deterministic code.

  • Collaboration and eagerness to learn: You thrive on direction, review, and challenge, take feedback well, and want to grow into larger scopes. You are eager to learn every day.

  • Going the extra mile: Be part of a high-growth phase, where we move fast and expect focused intensity. 9-to-5 is not the mode we work in, if you want to build something that matters with a team that ships, we are your people.

What We Offer

  • Ownership from day one: Real features running in production at major financial institutions, with the trust to carry them there yourself.

  • Founder collaboration: Work directly with founders who have built and scaled fintech and analytics products before.

  • We win and lose together as a team: We expect people to leave their comfort zone on a daily basis, however, we work together as a team and support each other at any time.

  • Growth: A dedicated development budget, free to use for whatever gives you a level-up.

Culture: Strong focus on a healthy, high-performance team culture, ranging from regular team events and dinners to an inclusive, fast-paced team that grows together.

Our stack

  • Core Backend: Python 3.14, FastAPI, Pydantic, and SQLAlchemy 2.0 in a strict four-layer architecture, exposed as separate internal and external APIs.

  • Background processing: Containerized worker services and event-driven AWS Lambda orchestrators for email ingestion, document triaging, and action running.

  • AI Integration: AI orchestration deeply integrated into application landscape via AWS Bedrock, e.g., to extract information and drive agentic activity.

  • Data & Storage: Per-tenant Aurora MySQL in isolated subnets, S3 for document persistence, and an append-only ledger for auditability.

  • Platform: A multi-tenant AWS environment on ECS Fargate with strict per-tenant network and data isolation (VPC, NACLs, WAF), CloudFront + Cognito (Google SSO/JWT) and API Gateway (IAM) at the edge, defined as code in CloudFormation across dev/staging/prod accounts.

  • Frontend: React single-page app for the internal workbench.

  • Dev Workflow: uv, Ruff, ty, pytest (unit, integration, property-based), Docker, GitHub Actions, and heavy use of Agentic IDEs to accelerate feature shipping.

title: Backend Engineering Manager
description:
HEY THERE

At Yazio, we help millions of users every day on their journey to healthy nutrition and greater well-being. We're hiring a Backend Engineering Manager to lead our Backend Team, a small, senior team behind Yazio's API and all of the AI features in the app. This role is for an engineering manager who has led a team before and enjoys helping experienced engineers take full ownership of their work, including the conversations with Product.

 

Let's shape the future of nutrition together and make Yazio the most successful nutrition app worldwide!

 

This role is 100% remote and open to candidates based in Germany, Spain, Portugal or the UK.

YOUR MISSION

Our Backend Team works with the product squads across Yazio, including Monetization, Growth, Tracking Experience, Mobile Platform and Web, as well as Internal Tools and our CRM team. As its manager, you'll give the engineers the context and support they need to own their initiatives end to end, from planning through to conversations with each squad.

 

In your first year, you'll:

  • Take ownership of the team's rituals in your first couple of months (stand-ups, refinements, sprint planning, retros and a bi-weekly written sync) and keep improving how the team works

  • Build close working relationships with squad leads and product managers, so backend work is part of each squad's plans from the start of the quarter

  • Own the team's part of our OKR process: build the quarterly roadmap with the engineers and keep progress visible to the teams that depend on it

  • Grow the team through regular 1:1s, development goals and timely feedback, and step in early when accountability slips

  • Hire for the team as it grows, together with our Talent Acquisition team

  • Keep an eye on production: when an issue or outage comes up, make sure it gets to the right person and is resolved

YOUR PROFILE

You'll thrive here if:

  • You've led an engineering team with direct reports, and you've helped that team take on new responsibilities or change the way it works

  • Before moving into management, you spent several years as a senior backend engineer, so you're comfortable discussing system design, infrastructure and technical trade-offs with a very experienced team

  • You get results through your team: you coach engineers to make decisions and handle stakeholder conversations themselves, and you give them the room to do it

  • You're a clear, friendly communicator who stays calm under pressure, including during an outage

  • You build strong relationships with other leads and stakeholders, and you hold your ground when someone has a strong opinion while staying open to the best solution

  • You have a strong product mindset and connect the team's work to what users and the business need

  • You notice when a topic has gone quiet and follow up before it stalls

Bonus points for:

  • Leading a team that supports several product squads at the same time

  • Working on high-traffic consumer products

  • Setting up, or working in, a model where backend engineers are embedded in product squads

  • Steering the business with KPIs and running A/B tests to improve them

 

OUR CORE TECH STACK

  • Backend: PHP (REST APIs) and Go (async processing and high-concurrency features)

  • Ways of working: Jira and Notion, with a Scrum-like process

  • AI features: daily tips, meal summaries and food search by voice, text and image

  • AI in development: agentic coding as part of the team's everyday workflow

  • Scale: up to one million API requests per minute

WHY US?

  • An exciting product with millions of users in over 150 countries, driven by our mission to transform the world through healthy eating

  • A remote-first setup: work 100% from home, join a co-working space, or work abroad for several weeks per year

  • 30 vacation days to relax and recharge, plus 5 child sick days if your little one needs you

  • A focus-driven culture that values efficiency over long hours - no overtime expectations, and if it happens, you get that time back!

  • A high-impact environment where your work drives real change - short decision-making processes and no micromanagement

  • A team culture where ambition and balance go hand in hand, supported by strong connections - from our fully covered company retreat to team meetups and virtual coffee breaks

  • Tools and support to do your best work: MacBook, monitor, and €1,000 annual learning budget, plus regular feedback and career development

  • A truly international team with English as our company language and a shared commitment to growth and well-being - supported by Sunday Supplements and Nilo Health

DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION

At Yazio, we believe that diversity fuels innovation. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone, regardless of gender identity, race, religion, age, sexual orientation, or ability, feels valued and empowered. We celebrate different perspectives and actively encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply.

READY TO JOIN US?

Excited to take Yazio to the next level and help people worldwide lead healthier lives? We’d love to hear from you! Please send us:

  • Your CV in English

  • Any additional materials that showcase your work (e.g., LinkedIn profile, portfolio)

We believe small, highly skilled teams outperform large, fragmented organizations, and we are intentional about staying focused on impact, quality, and speed.

We operate with a flat org structure and value in-person collaboration, which helps ideas move faster, decisions stay grounded, and teams take full ownership of what they build.
Our values

Internal tooling is not a backlog item at Prelude — it's a strategic lever. As we scale from 50 to a much larger team, the speed at which engineering, ops, sales, support, and finance can operate depends on the tools we put in their hands.

Founded by former Google search engineers with PhDs in AI from ETH Zurich, DeepJudge helps legal teams unlock and apply the knowledge inside their organizations through world-class enterprise search and AI infrastructure – enabling them to automate workflows, build knowledge-powered applications, and turn institutional knowledge into a lasting advantage.

Headquartered in Switzerland with a growing team across North America and Europe, DeepJudge is shaping the future of how professional knowledge is discovered and applied.

At DeepJudge, we move with urgency, think rigorously, and work closely with our clients to build products that solve meaningful problems. If you want to help define how AI transforms professional knowledge work, we’d love to hear from you.

About the role:

We're looking for a Frontend Engineer who combines strong technical expertise with a deep appreciation for well-crafted UIs and seamless user experiences. You'll be instrumental in building the features that make our powerful product feel intuitive and delightful to use.

Our users, legal professionals, operate under pressure and deal with high-stakes knowledge. Your mission is to build experiences that reduce cognitive load, guide users to the information they need, and help them fully leverage our product's capabilities.

Attention to detail matters here, from structure and architecture to animations and micro-interactions.

You'll have significant ownership over frontend architecture decisions and a real opportunity to shape how we build our product as we scale.   • Participate in agile development processes

  • Stay up to date with the latest industry trends and technologies

  • Ensure UI decisions prioritize usability, accessibility, and reduced cognitive load for end users

  • Contribute to the evolution of the design system

  • Write tests and monitor frontend performance to ensure a reliable, fast experience

  • Proactively identify areas for improvement and contribute ideas beyond your immediate scope

You're a great fit if you:

  • Have 4+ years of experience building and maintaining production applications with real end users using modern frontend frameworks (we're using React)

  • Love creating consistent and enjoyable user experiences that guide users through legal research, document analysis, and workflow automation, delighting them at every interaction

  • Have solid TypeScript experience, are comfortable with generics, type inference, and building type-safe components

  • Have a sharp eye for pixel-perfect UIs and smooth micro-interactions that convey meaning and bring designs to life

  • Demonstrate strong communication skills, can clearly articulate technical and visual decisions, and enjoy in-depth discussions with other team members

  • Enjoy collaborating closely with the product team, understanding their vision, and elevating it by crafting user experiences that are both beautiful and functional

Bonus points for:

  • Experience with NextJS in production, including server-side rendering strategies, caching, and route architecture

  • Familiarity with Figma and design handoff workflows

  • Accessibility experience that ensures our product works for all user groups

  • Experience leading frontend initiatives or mentoring other developers

What you can look forward to:

  • Location: Office 5min walking distance from Zurich central station, where we primarily work on site

  • Collaborative and supportive work environment

  • Potential for professional growth and advancement within the company

  • Ownership and ability to impact the company, product, and culture

This would not be the right role for you if you:

  • View frontend as just "making things look pretty" rather than optimizing user experience and product value

  • Want strict requirements and prefer to work solely on what you are told

  • Prefer working in isolation rather than collaborating closely with design and product

  • You haven't yet owned significant frontend decisions, or you haven't developed strong opinions about frontend architecture

  • Prefer to work remote-first and don't value in-person collaboration

description:
Who We Are

Zefir is building an AI autopilot for home sales in Europe, starting in France: an AI agent runs the entire sale and purchase journey end-to-end, orchestrating local brokers, portals, buyers, and documents.

Backed by over $55 million from top-tier investors like Sequoia Capital, we're committed to accelerating life changes for millions of current and future European homeowners.

The role

As a Business Development Representative (BDR), you are the first commercial point of contact with our prospects. You join Zefir's Sales team and reach out to homeowners who have run a valuation on our website but have not booked an appointment yet.

The core of the role is reactivation: these homeowners showed interest, then stopped there. You are the one who gets them moving again, on the phone, one by one.

Your goal as a BDR: create the sales opportunities that feed our revenue directly.

What you will do

  • Handle around 100 calls per day, with a target of 3 to 4 meetings booked daily.

  • Run qualification calls of about 20 minutes: understand the client's project, present Zefir's value proposition, and book a follow-up meeting with an Account Executive.

  • Keep rigorous track of your pipeline and move leads through the Sales funnel.

  • Work closely with Account Executives to maximize conversion and contribute directly to Zefir's growth.

Career path

We are transparent on this. A BDR role can open the door to an Account Executive role internally, but there is no automatic progression and no guaranteed timeline. Any move depends on three things: performance, behavioral fit, and team needs.

What we can commit to: our Consumer Account Executives, the role a BDR grows into, and our Sales Managers are filled exclusively through internal mobility. We never open these roles externally. Top performers are rewarded, with uncapped variable pay and real visibility.

Who we are looking for

  • 0 to 2 years of experience. This role is designed for a junior profile who wants to learn sales on the phone, fast and in the fiel d.

  • Master's level graduate from a business school, an engineering school or a university, or a first experience as a BDR, SDR or sales rep in a structured environment.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication. Fluency in French is required. Fluent English is a plus, not a must-have.

  • Rigorous and well organized, able to sustain a high volume of client interactions over time.

  • Energized by performance and intensity, with a client and results orientation.

  • Resilient, and able to take feedback to improve quickly.

One honest note: this role is intense and repetitive by design. Around a hundred calls a day, every day, with rejection along the way. That is what makes you improve fast at sales, and it is not for everyone.

Compensation and working setup

  • €47K package: €35K base plus €12K of uncapped variable, on top of the BSPCE granted to everyone.

  • Three days on-site, two days of remote work per week, at our Le Peletier office in the 9th arrondissement. Being in the room matters on this role, you learn to sell by hearing others sell.

Hiring process

  • Screening: a first 15-minute conversation with a member of the Talent team.

  • Use case: two written questions (15 minutes of work) to send back within 4 days.

  • Role interview, at our offices: 60 minutes on the role with the Sales Manager.

  • Culture interview: 45 minutes with a member of the Sales team.


Benefits

The following is for permanent employees only. For other contracts (interns, apprentices, fixed-term..), please, check with your recruiter.

  • Competitive salary: You can run your own simulation with our salary calculator.

  • BSPCE (Stock Options): Available for everyone, with monthly vesting after year one, over a 4-year period.

  • Healthcare plan: Full coverage with Alan for team members, their partners, and children.

  • Office in Le Peletier, Paris (9th arrondissement): With flexible remote work options.

  • Swile meal card: €11 per worked day.

  • Swile mobility card: €45/month to support sustainable transportation (metro, carpooling, biking…).

  • Team events: Monthly Mixers to connect and share good times, and quarterly All Hands to celebrate wins across the company.

Our Operating Principles

🏔️ Steep Mountains Are Steep: Setting ambitious goals and working hard to achieve them.

🌊 Ride Reality: Actively seeking challenges and thriving by adapting flexibly to changes.

🏀 Play for the Front of the Jersey: Prioritizing team success over individual recognition.

Application & Process

We welcome applications from anyone, regardless of background, gender, sexual orientation, religion, age, or experience. Our team values authenticity and diverse perspectives.

For all roles, our interview process emphasizes hands-on exercises, case studies, or discussions about specific examples of your previous work. We ensure objectives and expectations are clearly communicated at every step.

title: Video Lead
description:
📈 Who We Are:

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair.

Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity.

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale.

In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

In short

We're looking for a Video Lead to shoot and edit for tem. Full-time, £70,000, based anywhere in the UK with shoots around the country.

tem connects businesses directly with the renewable generators that power them, which makes it an unusually diverse thing to film: solar and wind sites, the people who run them, the businesses buying from them, and the engineers building the technology in between. Here's some of what we've made so far: here, here, here and here.

The work we want to make

Two kinds of video, held to the same standard.

Considered films, where pacing, sound and framing carry the story and every shot is there for a reason. The kind someone who has never thought about energy watches to the end, because they've started to care about the person in it.

And social pieces that aren't templates: short cuts made with real intent, where the rhythm, timing, sound design and effects all serve the idea. Native to the platform, unmistakably crafted.

You'll move between the two in the same week without either one slipping.

If you're freelance - most of the best shooter-editors work for themselves, and we understand why. Here's what we'd want you to know.

This isn't corporate video. Generator stories, customer films, policy explainers, engineering pieces and people-led series - a social series one week, a customer film the next. When it's worth moving fast, we can go from idea to published within a week, if that’s what we collectively decide.

You'd be building something, not borrowing it. Rather than picking up someone else's style for a few weeks, you'd shape what tem's video looks and feels like, and build a body of work around it over years. You're expected, and encouraged, to argue when you see a better way.

Fewer feedback rounds. One brand, one small team, and a direct line to whoever wrote the brief. You learn tem once, properly.

The money. £70,000, stock options, paid holiday, and no invoices to chase or quiet months to plan around.

What you'll own

tem's video from first shot to final export: how it's planned, shot and cut, and how it looks and sounds across everything we publish. You'll sit in the Brand team and report into the Content Lead.

  • Shoots. Planning properly - schedule, kit, shot list, a recce where it's worth it - then staying alert on the day for what the plan couldn't know. Running most shoots solo, and knowing when a piece needs extra crew and when a phone and good instincts will do.

  • People. Most of the generators, engineers and finance directors you'll film have never been on camera. Putting them at ease and getting the real version of them is half the job.

  • The edit (around 70% of your week). Cutting, grading, mixing and titling in Premiere Pro. Giving short social pieces the same care as the long ones, letting the considered films breathe, and making something good from very little when there's no shoot.

  • Story and style. Turning a brief or rough idea into how it should be shot and sequenced, pushing back when you see a better version, and developing a visual language for tem video over time.

How we use AI (and how we don't)

We're not looking for someone to make AI-generated films - our content works because it's real. We use tools where they earn their place: transcription and paper edits, selects, audio clean-up, subtitles, cutdowns and versioning, the occasional fix in post, and pre-production like moodboards and storyboards. We want someone curious enough to try new tools, with the judgement to know when not to.

What we're looking for

Must haves

  • A portfolio, wherever it lives, that shows both halves: considered, human storytelling and social work cut with real intent.

  • A professional standard at both shooting and editing.

  • Speed without losing control.

  • The ability to plan and run a shoot yourself.

  • Good with people, on and off camera.

  • Sensible, hands-on use of AI tools in a real pipeline.

  • UK-based and happy to travel for shoots.

Bonus points

  • Premiere Pro, since it's what we cut in.

  • Colour, sound design or motion graphics beyond the basics.

  • A freelance or small-studio background.

  • An interest in energy, climate or tech.

What you get

  • £70,000 salary, reviewed twice a year.

  • Your say in what video kit we invest in for the content team.

  • Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission.

  • 25 days holiday plus public holidays (swap them for the ones that matter to you), and your birthday off.

  • Remote first and flexible working, with no internal meetings on Friday afternoons.

  • Up to £1,200 a year for your remote setup and £150 a month for wellbeing.

How to apply

  • Send us your work. Your portfolio plus two recent pieces, with a line on what you did on each via the application form.

  • A 30-minute conversation with Alex (Content Lead) and Chelsea.

  • A paid, one-hour edit challenge. We send you unreleased tem footage, you cut it, and we talk through your choices. Everyone who delivers an edit at this stage is paid £200, hired or not - we don't think ideas should be taken for free.

  • A final conversation with leadership.

Reading this and know someone who'd be great? If we hire them, we'll pay you £1,000

Prelude is redefining how companies authenticate and onboard users - turning what's traditionally a cost center into a growth lever.

Founded in 2022 by former Zenly team members who lived the pain of broken SMS authentication firsthand, we're already serving fast-growing companies across Europe and are expanding into the US.

But authentication is only the starting point - we're building the platform for trust at scale, with an ambitious roadmap of market-defining products ahead.

Why join us

Today, we're a team of 60 and growing, based in Paris, building products that power secure and high-performance user onboarding for companies across the world. We believe small, highly skilled teams outperform large, fragmented organizations, and we are intentional about staying focused on impact, quality, and speed.

We operate with a flat org structure and value in-person collaboration, which helps ideas move faster, decisions stay grounded, and teams take full ownership of what they build.
Our values

  • Care
    We care deeply about our customers, our teammates, and the quality and reliability of what we ship.

  • Bias for Action
    We move fast, test in the real world, and iterate quickly rather than over-optimizing in theory.

  • Ownership
    We take responsibility end to end, from identifying problems to delivering outcomes and learning from results.

About the Role

As a Mid-Market Account Executive, you'll be responsible for driving growth across one of Prelude’s most strategic segments: mid-sized businesses with high-scale authentication needs. You’ll own the full sales cycle, manage complex evaluations with multiple stakeholders, and partner closely with our technical teams to deliver high-impact solutions.

You’ll help shape our mid-market motion, refine our GTM strategy, and play a meaningful role in expanding Prelude’s footprint across Europe and beyond. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who has experience closing mid-market deals and wants to join a fast-growing startup where their impact is immediate and visible.

What will you be doing?

• Owning and managing the sales cycle for mid-market accounts, from outbound prospecting to contract execution.

• Building and maintaining a strong pipeline of high-value prospects across key verticals.

• Leading consultative discovery processes to understand customer needs, technical requirements, and decision criteria.

• Navigating multiple stakeholders — from product and engineering to procurement and legal.

• Consistently exceeding quota while maintaining healthy win rates and sales velocity.

• Delivering on cross-sell, up-sell and renewal opportunities

• Sharing insights from customer interactions to help refine product strategy, messaging, and positioning.

Who we are

Yubo is the Social Discovery app to make new friends and hang out online. By eliminating likes and follows, we empower our users to create genuine connections and show up as their true selves.

We've pioneered a new way for Gen Z to socialize online, and with millions of active users, our goal is to redefine how we connect today and tomorrow.

Our team is international, multicultural and deeply committed to its mission. As the leading platform to socialize online, we have a special responsibility to build a safe digital space for our community. Safety is embedded in our DNA, and our proactive approach focuses on user protection, support, and education. We also work closely with the broader technology industry to share our knowledge and NGOs create industry-leading child protection standards.

Join us in this exciting journey and help us shape the future of social interactions!

About this role:

At Yubo, design has a real seat at the table. It leads squads in partnership with Product Management and Engineering, shaping strategy and decisions from ideation all the way to delivery, with direct and visible impact on both the product and the business.

We're precisely looking for a Mobile Product Designer to co-lead one of our Product Squad. This is a highly strategic role where you'll help shape product strategy, design experiments, and deliver end-to-end product initiatives focused on impacting growth, retention, and monetization across a product used by millions of users.

You'll spend time understanding user behaviour, exploring solutions, validating ideas, and refining experiences based on real-world data, all for the sake of shipping quality experiences. We don’t expect everything to be perfect from the get-go though, so expect iteration at every occasion!

This role is particularly well suited to someone who enjoys balancing product thinking with strong craft, and who wants their work to have a visible impact on business outcomes and user experience alike.

Like what you’re reading already? I think you’ll enjoy what follows.

Your responsibilites

  • Lead product design projects from discovery through delivery and post-launch iteration

  • Partner closely with Product Managers, Engineers, Brand Marketing, Data Analysts, Legal and Trust&Safety to solve meaningful user problems

  • Contribute to product strategy, experimentation, and roadmap discussions

  • Design mobile-first experiences across iOS and Android with strong attention to usability, accessibility, and visual quality

  • Translate user needs, business goals, and technical constraints into thoughtful product experiences

  • Use analytics, feedback and competitive insights to formulate design decisions

  • Create prototypes and test concepts to validate ideas quickly

  • Help evolve and maintain Yubo's design system and contribute to design consistency across the product

  • Advocate for high-quality user experiences while remaining pragmatic about delivery and iteration

Tools we use:

  • Figma

  • Amplitude

  • Notion

  • Enterpret

  • Slack

  • AI tooling: Dust, Claude Code / Codex (prototyping & daily workflow)

Who you are:

  • You have 3-4+ years of experience designing digital products, ideally within consumer mobile applications

  • You are comfortable owning projects from problem definition through launch

  • You combine strong visual design skills with solid product thinking

  • You know how to use data, research, and user feedback to guide decisions

  • You can communicate design rationale clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders

  • You enjoy collaborating closely with Product and Engineering teams

  • You are comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities can evolve

  • You have the conviction to make bold design calls and defend them

  • You design with the user at the center

  • Experience with social, community, social discovery, gaming, or consumer subscription products is a plus

Within a month, you will:

  • Get familiar with Yubo's product, users, business model, and design principles

  • Build relationships with your Product Squad and key stakeholders across Product, Engineering, Data, Brand, Trust&Safety

  • Understand current product priorities, ongoing experiments, and major user journeys

  • Learn how we use data and research to make product decisions

  • Start contributing to design discussions and smaller initiatives

Within 6 months, you will:

  • Own the design of your squad's key initiatives end to end, from discovery and experimentation to polished, shipped mobile experiences that move your squad's objectives.

  • Use data, user insight and experimentation to frame problems, validate your design decisions, and measure their impact after launch.

  • Contribute beyond your squad to the broader design team, raising the craft bar, strengthening our design system, and influencing product decisions across the company.

The recruitment process

  • Phone screen with Nicolas, Talent Acquisition

  • First interview with Sacha, our CEO

  • Case Study and debrief with the Design team

  • Cultural fit assessments

  • And if everything went well, an offer!

What we offer

  • A highly competitive salary range as well as equity in the company

  • A highly flexible remote work policy, 2 days at the office per month, with monthly team events.

  • We also cover fees for external professional events and meetups (Android Makers, etc…)

  • Great health insurance coverage for both you and your family by Alan, fully paid for by Yubo !

  • Numerous benefits for parents: additional parental leave, easy access to nurseries and daycare facilities in France.

Our approach to privacy & safety

As part of your role, you may handle tools and features involving personal data. We expect all employees to demonstrate strong awareness of privacy and safety issues, and to actively support our Privacy & Safety by Design efforts.

Join Yubo and help shape the future of Social Discovery while enjoying a culture that values flexibility, well-being, and impact.

You own the impact: Step up, adapt, and make it matter

One team, one mission: No egos, no passengers, just shared wins

title: Senior / Staff Product Engineer
description:
About Passionfroot

Creator-led growth is one of the fastest-growing channels in B2B—and we’re building the infrastructure behind it.

Passionfroot is the leading platform where modern companies scale creator-led growth, and where top creators manage and monetize brand partnerships.

Our customers include some of the most ambitious, fastest-moving companies in the world—Replit, HubSpot, Figma, Cursor, Gamma, Attio, Intercom, and ElevenLabs. We help them run high-impact creator programs across LinkedIn, YouTube, newsletters, and more.

We're growing 13x in revenue year over year, profitable, and just closed our Series A round! We are backed by leading investors including Insight Partners, Creandum, Supernode and founders and operators from Cursor, Anthropic, n8n and more. We're expanding fast across New York, Europe, and Brazil - and we're just getting started.

We’re still a small team, which means the people who join now will have an outsized influence on the product, the engineering culture, and the company we become.

About the role

We’re looking for a Senior or Staff Product Engineer to help build the next generation of Passionfroot.

You’ll work across the full stack on both our core platform and Zest, our AI Campaign Manager for creator marketing. That could mean designing a new workflow for managing creator campaigns, making collaboration data feel instant, or turning models, search, and product context into a reliable AI experience that customers can trust.

We don’t separate “AI engineering” from “product engineering.” AI is becoming part of how the product works, but great product fundamentals still matter: understanding the user, shaping the problem, choosing the right architecture, building a thoughtful experience, and operating it reliably in production.

You’ll work closely with the founders, design, and customers to take important problems from early exploration to shipped product.

We’re a team of six engineers, and staying small is deliberate. It means you can have an idea on Monday and have customers using it by Thursday—without layers of sprint ceremonies or alignment meetings in between. The flip side is real ownership: you need to exercise strong judgment, communicate your decisions, and think through their consequences rather than wait for someone else to catch them.

📍This role is based in our Berlin or São Paulo offices with a hybrid work model. We are also open to candidates who are willing to relocate to either area.

What you’ll do

  • Own meaningful product areas from problem definition through architecture, implementation, launch, and iteration.

  • Build customer-facing features across our marketplace, campaign management, collaboration, payments, analytics, and creator workflows.

  • Help make Zest an indispensable part of how modern companies run creator-led growth.

  • Turn foundation models into structured, reliable product experiences—not just impressive prototypes.

  • Work on intelligent workflows involving agents, tools, retrieval, search, recommendations, and generated interfaces.

  • Develop the evaluations, observability, and feedback loops needed to understand whether AI features are genuinely useful.

  • Work closely with design to create experiences that are fast, intuitive, and polished.

  • Talk directly with customers and translate ambiguous needs into simple product decisions.

  • Make pragmatic architectural choices that balance speed, quality, maintainability, and performance.

  • Improve the systems and engineering practices that help a small team ship reliably at high velocity.

  • At Staff level, provide technical direction across projects, raise the engineering bar, and help other engineers make better decisions.

What we’re looking for

  • Significant experience building and shipping high-quality, customer-facing software. 5+ years is a useful guide, but the scope and quality of your work matter more than the number.

  • Strong TypeScript and React fundamentals, with experience working across the full stack.

  • A track record of independently driving complex features or products from an ambiguous starting point to measurable customer impact. When you encounter a blocker, you investigate, communicate, and find another path forward without waiting to be managed.

  • Strong product and technical judgment. You care about what should be built, how it should feel, and whether it actually solves the problem. You can distinguish between problems that need a sophisticated system and problems that need a simple, well-executed solution.

  • Experience building with LLMs or other applied AI systems in production.

  • An understanding of the challenges behind reliable AI products: evaluation, context, retrieval, model behavior, latency, cost, observability, and failure modes.

  • Clear, proactive communication and the ability to collaborate effectively in a remote environment.

  • Care for software craftsmanship without losing sight of momentum and customer outcomes.

Our technology

Passionfroot is built primarily in TypeScript across the full stack.

Our core product uses React, Remix, PostgreSQL, Prisma, and Zero sync for real-time product experiences. Our AI systems use foundation models from multiple providers alongside the AI SDK, Typesense, and Laminar for search, agent workflows, evaluations, and observability.

You don’t need experience with everything we use. We care more about strong fundamentals, relevant product experience, and your ability to learn quickly.

What success looks like

Within your first months, you will have:

  • Developed a deep understanding of creator-led growth and the problems our customers face.

  • Taken ownership of a major product or technical area with limited oversight.

  • Improved how we build, evaluate, and operate AI-powered functionality.

  • Earned the trust of the team through reliable execution and clear communication.

  • Helped us make better product and technical decisions beyond your immediate projects.

Our interview process

We want the process to be useful, respectful, and representative of how we actually work. We don’t use take-home challenges or algorithmic whiteboard interviews.

The process typically includes:

  1. A short introductory call.

  2. A conversation with Lorenzo about your experience, ambitions, and the work you are most proud of.

  3. A technical walkthrough of a project you know deeply, focused on the decisions and trade-offs you made.

  4. A collaborative product and technical problem-solving session with members of the team.

  5. A paid work trial based on a realistic problem, which can be completed flexibly around your current commitments.

  6. References and offer.

We aim to complete the process within one to two weeks.

What we offer

  • Competitive salary and equity in a Series A company.

  • Remote-first work with the option to work together in Berlin if you are local.

  • Latest Apple hardware and the tools you need to do your best work.

  • 25 days of paid vacation, plus local public holidays.

  • Regular team events and off-sites—past destinations include Mallorca, Barcelona, the South of France, Berlin, and the Baltic Sea.

description:

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

About the role

As a Senior Frontend Engineer on our Website team, you'll be a co-owner of the platform behind synthesia.io: the component library, content model and rendering stack that every page on our marketing site is built from. You'll shape direction and make key technical decisions with the team, likely with a focus area of your own but context across the whole system. This is a hands-on engineering role, and your primary output is high-quality component and schema code, plus the tooling that lets others build with it.

Millions of people visit synthesia.io every month, and it is one of the main ways we win new customers. That comes with real responsibility. The decisions you make are seen at scale, and we set the quality bar accordingly.

The defining challenge of this role is composability: a marketing site that marketers, and increasingly AI agents, can build pages with, without breaking design, performance or SEO.

You can expect to:

  • Build, scale and evolve our section library: the Astro components, Sanity schemas and design tokens that let us compose marketing pages consistently and accessibly.

  • Own the content model. Design schemas that resist misuse, so an editor, or an agent, can build a page that is correct by construction rather than correct by review.

  • Take Figma component specs all the way to production: responsive across mobile, tablet and desktop, accessible by default, matching design intent precisely.

  • Extend the platform for AI-assisted development, so coding agents can generate on-brand, on-spec sections from a design spec as reliably as a person can.

  • Own SEO integrity as a first-class engineering concern: canonicals, sitemaps, structured data, redirects, and no traffic cliffs on launch.

  • Raise the bar on engineering standards across the website surface: thorough code review, patterns others can follow, and tests around the parts that actually break.

  • Maintain and extend localisation across nine locales and a translation pipeline, so the system works for a global audience.

  • Shape the technical direction of the website platform over the next 6 to 12 months, and champion its adoption with the people who publish on it.

What we're looking for

  • At least five (5) years as a software engineer, including three (3) at senior level, building front end for content-driven or marketing platforms.

  • Real ownership of a content model in Sanity. You've designed schemas other people had to live with, and you have opinions about references vs. embedded objects, when a variant belongs in the schema versus at runtime, and how to stop a section library sprawling. GROQ and Portable Text are familiar territory.

  • Deep front-end expertise: expert HTML, CSS and TypeScript, with a strong command of component API design and the developer experience of a shared library.

  • You can work end to end. Comfortable owning the server side as well as the front end: SSR, serverless and edge runtimes, API routes, a SQL database, secrets and CI. You should be able to take a feature from schema to component to the route that serves it without handing off, and be happy debugging something that only reproduces in production.

  • Solid understanding of responsive design, cross-browser compatibility and web performance, and comfortable building to WCAG 2.2 AA. Accessibility is part of your definition of done, not a separate pass.

  • You care that marketing sites are measured, on performance, SEO, analytics events and conversion, and you're happy being accountable to those numbers.

  • A strong sense of craft and attention to detail, and the judgement to balance design intent against engineering constraints.

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills. You explain your reasoning, review generously, and treat levelling up the people around you as part of the job.

Nice to haves

  • Prior experience working on a large SaaS marketing website, at real traffic and with real stakes attached.

  • Astro, or another islands or static-site framework.

  • Cloudflare Workers, or another edge or serverless platform.

  • Experience with AWS Lambda.

  • Tailwind CSS v4, and experience working from a token-based design system.

  • Experience, or strong interest, in making component libraries and content models consumable by AI agents.

  • A strong design sensibility: an eye for visual detail and the judgement to push back on and improve design decisions, not just build them.

  • Experience with localisation and internationalisation at scale for a global audience.

  • Analytics and tag management implementation: dataLayer events, server-side tagging, getting attribution right without hurting performance.

Our culture

At Synthesia we're passionate about building, not talking, planning or politicising. We strive to hire the smartest, kindest and most unrelenting people and let them do their best work without distractions. Our work principles serve as our charter for how we make decisions, give feedback and structure our work to empower everyone to go as fast as possible. You can find out more about these principles here.

The hiring process:

  • 30 min call with our Technical Recruiter

  • 45 min call with the Head of Website about your past projects

  • 75 min practical exercise with one of our engineers. We hand you a real Figma section spec and work through how you'd model and build it. Collaborative, not Leetcode.

  • 60 min call with leadership, focused on examples of collaboration, growth, and the details of your future team.

Other important info:

  • Our preference is for this role to be based either in-office or remote in London, UK. We can also accommodate remote workers elsewhere in Europe subject to compliance and right to work checks.

  • This is full-time employment only, usually through OysterHR. No contractors possible.

Across all three, you build the reusable kit that makes this repeatable: scoping templates, architecture patterns, and a procurement answer library.

Objectives

  • 90 days: own scoping and procurement response for active deals, with the reusable kit used on at least one live deal end to end.

  • You are technically credible: you read code, reason fluently about integrations and the MCP and agent stack, and can scope and oversee a deployment. This is not a hands-on production-coding role; implementation is handled by our freelancer network.

  • You have an interest in the MCP and agent stack.

  • You are open to traveling from time to time across Europe and the US to meet clients.

  • A backend engineering role. You will work with clients most of the week.

title: Remote Head of UX (m/f/d)
description:
About RoomPriceGenie ✨🧞‍♂️

Founded in 2017, RoomPriceGenie is dedicated to helping hoteliers around the globe achieve optimal pricing. 🌍 We understand that many small hotels face challenges with digitalization, making their operations increasingly complex and often resulting in lost revenue. This is where we come in!

We have developed a powerful solution that enables hotels to set the right prices in just seconds. ⏱️ Our state-of-the-art algorithm analyzes both internal hotel data and market trends to recommend pricing strategies that enhance revenue and improve booking rates.

With customers spanning the globe—from the USA and Canada to Iceland, South Africa, China, Slovenia, Italy, and the UK—RoomPriceGenie has made a meaningful impact in the hospitality industry, and our clients love the results. ❤️

Now, we are excited to expand our customer base and spread the word about how we can support hoteliers in optimizing their pricing strategies. We invite you to join us on this journey! We actively encourage applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds to enrich our team and drive innovation.

Your Role

As the Head of UX at RoomPriceGenie, you'll lead our small but mighty design and research team of two product designers and one user researcher.

This isn't an IC role where you'll be pushing pixels or running sessions yourself. It's a leadership role focused on building the function, championing the team, and setting them up for success.

You'll set the strategic direction for how design and research operates, advocate for the team at leadership level, and create the conditions for your people to do their best work. You'll also play a key role in raising design and research maturity across the wider product organisation — guiding better decisions through clearer systems, guidelines, and shared insight.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership Representation & Advocacy

  • Champion design and research as a strategic partner that shapes the roadmap.

  • Partner with Product Leadership to translate strategic business priorities into a clear, sequenced roadmap for Design & Research.

Strategic Direction & Vision

  • Set a clear vision for the design and research function — defining what success looks like, where it's heading, and how it contributes to the company's overall strategy.

  • Raise design and research maturity by providing constructive critique and quality oversight to support high-quality product outcomes.

  • Create the space for the team to work on foundational initiatives that scale team impact. For example: evolving the component library into a robust design system and establishing clear design and content playbooks to drive consistency, efficiency, and quality.

AI Operations & Enablement

  • Set the strategic direction for how AI fits into the design & research workflow — where it accelerates, where craft stays human, and set clear guardrails for how the wider org uses it.

  • Foster a culture where the team integrates AI into product work — evolving their craft and building fluency through practice.

  • Ensure designers and researchers play a key role in shaping product and AI direction, grounding decisions in user insight and design perspective.

Stakeholder Collaboration

  • Advocate for Design Thinking to be embedded throughout the product life cycle, shaping ideas and guiding decisions.

  • Proactively identify large, strategic UX opportunities that span across the product.

  • Navigate competing priorities between leadership direction and team capacity, ensuring the team stays focused on high-impact work.

Team Development & Coaching

  • Provide ongoing coaching, mentoring, and constructive feedback through regular one-to-ones — focused on the development and growth of your team.

  • Build clear career frameworks and progression paths for Design and Research.

  • Encourage continuous learning, adaptability, and development within the team.

Your Profile

  • A genuine understanding of both design and research disciplines, even if your background leans more toward one. You don't need to be an expert in both, but you need to value and support both equally.

  • Proven experience in a senior design leadership role is required — you've owned a function, led teams of designers and researchers, and have a track record of influencing product direction at the leadership level.

  • A track record of advocating for both disciplines at the leadership level and influencing product strategy, not just delivering on it.

  • Experience building or maturing a design function: establishing processes, systems, playbooks, or ways of working from the ground up.

  • Curiosity about AI and how it's changing the way design and research teams work — you don't need to be an expert, but you should be excited about figuring this out with the team.

Your Soft Skills

  • A compassionate, proactive leadership style that creates emotional safety for the people around you.

  • Confident navigating difficult stakeholder dynamics without losing your composure or your team's trust.

  • Strong communicator who can translate design value into language that resonates with leadership, product, and engineering.

  • Comfortable giving and receiving direct feedback — you see it as a gift.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in or familiarity with the hotel or travel industry.

  • Familiarity with building or scaling teams.

  • Experience building and maintaining a design system.

  • Experience working in scale-ups or startups — you're comfortable with ambiguity and thrive in environments that are still finding their shape.

What We Offer at RoomPriceGenie 💪

At RoomPriceGenie, we don’t just offer jobs; we offer an adventure! 🚀 Join us in an exciting startup atmosphere where you can grow your career while changing the world for tens of thousands of independent hoteliers. 🌍 Our global and diverse team is fueled by passion and a shared mission. We thrive in a culture that’s all about transparency, respect, and making a real impact together.

  • Growth and Development: We’re all about lifelong learning! 📚 Level up your skills with personal and professional development opportunities. You’ll even snag up to three extra days off each year to focus on your growth. 📈

title: Associate Product Owner
description:
TL;DR

Full-time. Berlin-based. No remote option available for this role. You sit with the PM.

Join GlassDollar as an Associate Product Owner and own the space between a good idea and a shipped feature.
Someone has to decide what "done" means, write it down clearly enough that an engineer can start on Monday, and stay close enough to the build that the scope does not quietly grow on the way. That is the job. You own it end to end: specs, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and a backlog that keeps everyone honest about what is actually shipping. Nobody hands you a ticket queue you did not write yourself.

The problem you'll be solvingA corporation with 100,000 employees has thousands of expensive operational problems, and somewhere out there a startup has already solved most of them. Getting those two facts to meet is slow, political, and mostly attempted in spreadsheets that die in someone's downloads folder.
GlassDollar OS is the venture clienting platform that makes it repeatable: sourcing the startups, matching them to real problems, running the pilots, and rolling out what works across the whole organisation. Enterprise customers run real innovation budgets through it. What you scope this month decides what they can do next quarter.


What we're looking for

You have personally written the tickets.
3+ years in a product company, where scoping and ticket-writing were actually your job rather than something you handed off.
You are technical enough to argue with engineers.
AI models, API contracts, estimates, sequencing. You push back with reasons, and you change your mind when the reasons coming back are better.
You can write.
A spec is a piece of writing. We will ask for a sample where the reasoning is visible, polish second.
You write specs worth acting on.
The valuable ones pull three threads together: where the product is going, what clients are actually telling us, and the knowledge already sitting in the team. You gather all three before you write, so what lands on the board is specific enough to build and pointed enough to matter.
You know what looks good.
You have a great sense of design and what feels good for users. We will ask you to build a prototype with AI and illustrate the specs visually.
You have worked somewhere small enough that there was nowhere to hide.
No layers between you and the consequences of a bad spec.
You want to be coached hard.
Direct feedback, weekly, on your actual work. You will scope alongside the product lead until you are doing it alone, and the goal is that this happens fast.
You are fluent with AI tooling, day to day.
We want to see the workflow, not hear it described.
You want the scope to grow.
The people who do best here end up owning areas outright: the major initiatives, the roadmap arguments, and the questions everyone else brings their doubts to. That is earned, and it is genuinely available.


What you'll do

Your job: turn validated opportunities into work an engineer can start on Monday.

  • Turning opportunities into scoped, sequenced, estimable work: specs, acceptance criteria, edge cases, dependencies
  • Running the backlog: grooming, prioritisation input, keeping the board honest about what is in flight, blocked, or quietly drifting
  • Being the interface between customer signal (support threads, CS conversations, call notes) and the engineering queue
  • Coordinating releases and checking that what shipped matches what was scoped
  • Presenting product decisions to varied stakeholder groups, from engineers to enterprise clients

What you'll be scoping over your first year:
  • Deep integrations into our customers' organisations. Their systems, their data, their identity stack. This is the work that turns GlassDollar from a tool people visit into infrastructure they run on.
  • Public REST APIs and MCP servers, so our customers' engineers and their AI agents can build on top of us.
  • AI embedded across the product, inside the surfaces people already work in.
  • Workflow automation inside the platform, so the work that used to take six meetings and a shared spreadsheet runs itself.
You will need to understand each of these well enough to write the spec and defend it in the room.
This is a doing role rather than a people-management one. Mid-to-senior individual contributor.


Requirements

  • 3+ years in a product company, where you personally wrote the tickets
  • Technical enough to understand a data model, an API contract, and estimation
  • Demonstrable writing ability, be ready to share a spec, PRD or decision doc
Nice to have:
  • B2B enterprise SaaS background
  • Familiarity with venture clienting, corporate innovation, or startup-scouting workflows
  • Notion fluency

Don't check every box? Apply anyway. We care more about the questions you ask about a brief than the answer you land on.


How we hire

Straightforward. Respectful of your time. No mystery steps.

  1. Intro call: a quick chat to see if there's a match
  2. Interview with the PM, including a brief introduction to the work sample: a spec, PRD, or decision doc where your reasoning is visible, plus examples of problems you've framed
  3. Interview
  4. Offer: if it clicks, we don't wait around
