title: Engineering Manager
description:
🏆 What's the opportunity?

Air freight carries less than 1% of world trade by volume and more than a third of it by value, around $22.7 billion of goods every single day. It's how a vaccine reaches a clinic before it spoils, how a semiconductor arrives before the production line stops, and how a retailer restocks a continent away in three days instead of five weeks. When speed is the whole point, freight flies.

Somebody has to price it, book it and move it, and that work is still done largely by hand, in inboxes and spreadsheets.

For eight years we've been building the data infrastructure underneath it: direct integrations with 75 airlines, the top ten ocean carriers and dozens of GSAs, used every day by 30,000 freight forwarders across 172 countries to hold their rates, price their business and book their freight.

In 2026 we acquired Cargofive, and cargo.one now spans air and ocean, the two modes that carry international trade. That foundation is what makes the next part possible.

In March 2026 we launched the industry's first AI-native operating system for multimodal freight:one workspace where freight teams and AI agents work side by side across rate management, procurement, quoting, booking and support. Crane Worldwide and Yusen Logistics are rolling it out across their global operations.

AI-led engineering is how we build. Engineers write specs and acceptance criteria, agents do much of the implementation, and the engineer owns the architecture, the review and what ships.

We're backed by Index Ventures, Bessemer, Creandum, Point Nine, Next47 and Lufthansa Cargo, which has been an investor in us since 2018.

🚀 What makes this role different

This is an engineering management job for a team where agents do much of the implementation. That changes the job.

When producing code gets cheaper and faster, the bottleneck moves. Throughput depends more on how well engineers define the problem, direct the agents, review what comes back and tell a plausible answer from a correct one.

You'll lead our engineers: what they ship, how good it is, how fast they move, whether the people are growing, and how quickly the team gets better at working AI-led. A lot of what engineering managers know about pacing, estimating, reviewing and measuring a team was calibrated for a different bottleneck. Working out what good looks like now is part of this job.

Today, engineers direct agents on their own work. That's where we are, but it's not the end state. We're building toward fleets of agents that work on their own inside guardrails and harnesses we design, while engineers move up to setting direction, reviewing what comes back, and owning what ships. Part of your job is helping the team get there while keeping the quality bar high.

This is also a player-coach role. You'll stay close enough to the code to keep your judgment sharp and your technical credibility current, while the engineers you lead and what they deliver remain the focus.

🧭 What we're looking for — the part that isn't negotiable

You get more from growing people than from being the smartest person in the room. You've watched someone you managed become better than you at something and enjoyed it. You run real one-to-ones, not status meetings. You give hard feedback early and kindly, and you've done the hard version more than once.

You think in systems. Teams are systems too. You can see why delivery is slipping without needing someone to tell you, and you fix the process rather than working harder inside a broken one.

You're excited about the business. You want to know what your engineers' work is worth and what it does for the customer paying us. You can explain that to them so their work has a point beyond the issue they're closing.

You work at eye level with Product. You co-own what gets built and when, push back on the brief, and don't treat "Product decides, Engineering delivers" as a healthy way to work.

You want to be in the room with customers. Freight forwarders and airlines, directly. You'd rather hear the problem first-hand, and you take your engineers with you.

English is your working language, at close to native fluency. You write and speak it the way you think in it. Almost everything a manager does in a remote-first company is language: the feedback that has to land precisely, the written decision that stops a debate, the difficult conversation where the wrong word costs you trust.

You'll also need:

  • Experience managing engineers: hiring them, growing them, running performance honestly and shipping on a predictable cadence.

  • A backend engineering background, strong architecture instincts and enough technical currency that your engineers respect your technical opinion.

  • A delivery track record. Specific things that shipped, on a schedule you can describe, and an honest account of what slipped and why.

  • Experience building a team, not only running one. You know how to assess for potential, close a candidate and set someone up so their first ninety days work.

  • Genuine engagement with AI-led engineering. You don't need to be an expert, but you can't manage engineers working this way from the outside. You need to use the tools yourself and want to get good at them.

  • Judgment, and the nerve to use it. You'll make calls with incomplete information and own them out loud.

  • Low ego. You take feedback from your own engineers and change your mind in public.

Nice to have: experience with our stack of Python 3, Flask, gRPC, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery and Kubernetes on GCP; Vue.js; managing a distributed team across several countries; or introducing a new way of working to a team that didn't ask for one.

🎬 A snapshot of what you'll be doing

  • Own delivery. What ships, how good it is and whether the commitments you make hold.

  • Grow the people. One-to-ones that are worth the hour, honest performance conversations, career paths that mean something, and knowing what each person wants next.

  • Hire. You'll own the hiring bar and run your own loops. We hire senior engineers on judgement and character rather than AI experience, and teach them the workflow. You'll be central to making that work.

  • Partner with Product as an equal. Shape the roadmap, negotiate scope and protect engineers from churn that isn't worth it.

  • Raise the team's AI capability. Help engineers use agents better today, spread what works, remove friction, and help evolve our setup toward autonomous agent fleets with the right guardrails and harnesses in place.

  • Stay technical, roughly a day a week. Reviews, a well-chosen piece of work, enough to keep your hands and judgement in.

  • Go to the users. Sit with freight forwarders and airlines, and take your engineers with you.

🤖 What you'd be working with

We're honest about where we are: Everything below is real and running today, but some of it is young, adoption is uneven across our five teams, and the next stage doesn't exist yet. You'd help build it, not inherit it.

How we work AI-led:

  • Work starts from a spec: Tickets and specs are drafted with agent help, against our agreed templates. Once a spec meets the bar, engineers pick it up, refine it, and own the design and architecture decisions; only then do agents start implementing.

  • Conventions for how agents get context, how work runs in parallel, and how the results come back together safely.

  • AI review on every merge request in CI, and a human review standard built for telling a plausible answer from a correct one.

What we've built to make that work:

  • Our shared AI engineering practice: spec templates, a directory of reusable AI skills, agent harnesses and review conventions for giving agents context, running work in parallel and bringing the results back together safely.

  • A Slack-triggered agent (Timber) that takes a Jira ticket and delivers a merge request, currently handling all bugs and small, well-scoped tickets and built on our RAG context layer and a memory layer.

  • A triage agent that protects the team's focus: it routes incoming questions, tickets and reports from other internal teams to the right engineering team and does the first level of triage itself; answering directly, creating a bug ticket, or escalating to a human.

The furthest edge of this is our AI team's production work, the bar the rest of the practice is being pulled toward, and closing that gap across the department is part of your job:

  • AI doing commercial work in production. In June 2026, Saudia Cargo went live with an AI worker our engineers built. It handles inbound rate requests around the clock and returns a quote in seconds, cutting turnaround time by 68% with 89% first-time accuracy.

  • An LLM pipeline turning airlines' free-text email replies into structured, bookable quotes.

❤️ How we work

  • Feedback is constant and direct, in both directions. You'll get it in your first week and you're expected to give it.

  • Remote-first, which means we write things down.

  • You take ownership, and you back your opinions with data.

  • Given the ambitious option and the easy one, you take the ambitious one.

  • Diverse, and playful about it.

✨ What we offer

  • Equity in cargo.one. This role is equity-eligible.

  • Company-provided Claude Code and the other AI tools the work requires.

  • A one-time €650 home office budget, plus your choice of MacBook or Dell laptop, delivered before day one.

  • Co-working access through our partner Desana.

No battery, no retrofitting: the device harvests energy from the temperature differential between radiator and room air (thermo-harvesting) and communicates over LoRaWAN.

The system runs at scale across multi-unit residential portfolios. Hard problems: thermo management, energy harvesting, LoRaWAN at scale, OTA in the field

Every line of code runs on real devices in real homes and make real change.

title: Go-to-Market Working Student (m/f/d)
description:
1KOMMA5°

At 1KOMMA5°, we pursue a clear vision: Living on wind and sunlight forever for free. To make this a reality, we are building the energy system of the future with Heartbeat AI. Want to be part of it?

We bring together regional craftsmanship and scalable software: We don't think of solar, batteries, heat pumps, and e-mobility as isolated components, but control them as an intelligent, integrated overall system in our virtual power plant. Directly connected to the electricity market – in real time, fully automated. This way, energy is used when it is available from renewables and particularly cost-effective. By 2030, our goal is to transition 1.5 million households to renewable energies. Over 3,000 people are working towards this every day, at more than 80 locations worldwide, from Finland to Australia.

Want to take responsibility and build solutions that truly matter? Apply now and help us shape the energy world of tomorrow.

Learn about our Product & Tech team!

Deine Position

Heartbeat AI is our energy optimisation platform that always provides our customers with the cleanest and cheapest energy. As a Working Student on the Go-to-Market team, you support our team in optimising the performance, positioning, and monetisation of Heartbeat AI across our markets. You'll work on projects that span multiple countries rather than being tied to a single one, giving you a broad view of how GTM strategy adapts (and doesn't) from market to market. You will support initiatives end-to-end and get hands-on exposure to how mature and growing markets are actually scaled, and your research and analysis will directly feed decisions that go to Product, Sales, and Marketing.

  • You support Heartbeat AI GTM efforts across multiple markets by pulling, structuring, and sanity-checking performance data across pricing, packaging, and positioning initiatives.
  • You help prepare pricing and packaging analyses across markets, flagging patterns, gaps, or differences.
  • You assist in researching new positioning angles, competitor moves, and market trends, turning them into short, usable summaries that can be compared across countries.
  • You build a foundational understanding of Heartbeat AI's unit economics by supporting the data work behind monetisation decisions in different markets.
  • You coordinate logistics and follow-ups with Product, Tech, Marketing, and Sales stakeholders across regions, and join relevant syncs to learn how those conversations happen.
  • You help maintain performance dashboards and trackers spanning multiple markets, keeping data current so the team can spot underperformance quickly, wherever it shows up.
  • You take ownership of clearly scoped tasks and small projects end to end, checking in proactively when priorities are unclear.
  • You report into the Go-to-Market Director but work closely with all the Go-to-Market team members across the globe.

Dein Profil

  • You are currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's programme, ideally in Business, Energy Economics or a related field, and can work around 15 to 20 hours per week alongside your studies.
  • You are curious about GTM, pricing, or product strategy and want to learn how monetisation decisions get made differently across markets in a scaling tech company.
  • You are structured and reliable: you follow through on tasks without being chased and flag early when something's blocked, even when juggling requests from more than one market team.
  • You are comfortable working with spreadsheets and data, and you're keen to build a genuine feel for numbers and unit economics rather than just running through checklists.
  • You communicate clearly and aren't afraid to ask questions or push back when something doesn't add up, even when talking to more senior stakeholders.
  • You are a fast learner who's comfortable picking up new tools and adapting to a fast-changing environment, and to working with different teams and cultures across markets.
  • You are fluent in English (C1/C2), written and verbal; additional European languages (German, Italian, Spanish, or others relevant to our markets) are a plus.
  • Prior exposure to the energy market or a tech/startup environment is a plus, but not a must.

Benefits

  • You are part of an international, dynamic, and highly motivated team of people who have proven to make things happen
  • With your work, you accelerate the "energy transition" and hence have a direct impact on our climate
  • Work with and learn from other super-smart colleagues
  • You will enjoy direct contact with core decision-makers
  • You will enjoy the best chances of entering full-time in one of Europe’s most thriving scaleups
  • You work remotely (Germany-wide), with offices in Hamburg, Berlin or Munich
  • Create a healthy balance alongside your work and enjoy all the benefits of the EGYM Wellpass
  • Benefits and discounts are yours with Futurebens

title: Special Projects Associate // London
description:
A Company That Matters

Insurance exists to support people at their most vulnerable, after an accident, illness, theft, fire, or crisis. Claims are the moment of truth. That's why we're passionate about making every claim more empathetic, more efficient, and more human.

ClaimSorted is an AI-native Third Party Administrator that manages claims operations for insurers across auto, property, travel, gadget, pet, renters, and liability. We combine world-class claims talent with proprietary AI systems to deliver dramatically faster resolutions, lower leakage, and a fundamentally better customer experience.

Backed by Y Combinator, Atomico, and Eurazeo, we've raised $16M+ and already manage more than $200M in insurance premium, including publicly traded companies and some of the most well-known household names.

The Role

You'll work directly with the founders on the things that hold a fast-growing company together: how we operate day to day, how we hire, and how it feels to join us. Broad scope, real ownership, from your first month.

  • Define how ClaimSorted operates day to day — the cadence, processes and tools that keep a fast-growing team coordinated as we scale.

  • Own the candidate and employee experience end to end, and build the systems that keep it consistently high.

  • Set the standard for how ClaimSorted communicates, internally and out — voice, templates, response times.

  • Act as the first filter on our hiring pipeline: run screening calls and shape the founders' shortlist.

We love working together in the office, so this is a full-time, office-based role in our London office. We're a high-intensity team and often put in significant time and effort, because we believe great outcomes come from doing the work well.

Qualifications

  • 0–3 years somewhere you had to organise people and juggle priorities — startup, accelerator, consulting, VC, or a previous founder associate seat.

  • You hold several priorities at once and know which one matters today.

  • You fix processes rather than absorbing them.

  • Naturally good with people, and quick to build rapport.

  • Excellent writing. Much of this role is writing on behalf of the company.

  • Proficient with AI tools.

Our Values

  • Move Fast – Act decisively, iterate quickly, optimise for momentum.

  • Always Overdeliver – We exceed expectations in everything we do.

  • Think Customer-First, Always – The customer experience drives every decision.

  • Challenge the Status Quo – We innovate relentlessly and never settle for 'good enough.'

  • Say It How It Is – Transparency and direct communication build trust.

title: Senior Frontend Engineer
description:
At Adapty, we make it easy for mobile apps to manage in-app purchases and paywalls. We power 20K+ apps, process $3B+ in subscriptions every year, and have been growing fast for the last four years. Our mission is simple: make apps rich.

We are a team of 210+ passionate, product-driven people who love solving big challenges. Backed by top investors like 500 Startups and Surface Ventures, we are building one of mobile's fastest-growing SaaS companies and aiming for number one worldwide.

Why This Role Matters

Flow Builder is one of Adapty's core products and the biggest bet we're making right now.

Our customers use it to assemble the screens their users see before paying: onboarding, quizzes, paywalls, and post-purchase experiences. They build multi-screen flows with branching, variables, and conditional content directly in the browser. The Adapty SDK renders those flows natively on iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter, and Capacitor, and a change published in the editor reaches users without an app release.

We're building the most capable native-rendering builder on the market, and that sets a high bar for engineering. This is an editor with the complexity of a design tool: a document model, a layer tree, layout and styling systems, a preview that has to agree with five runtimes, and an AI Editor that can rewrite the screen you're looking at from a prompt.

It's closer to Figma than to a dashboard, with subscription revenue running through every screen it renders.

We're hiring a Senior Frontend Engineer to own the frontend of Flow Builder and help shape what it becomes. You'd set architectural direction rather than pick up specced tickets, work with the SDK team on the config contract, and take features from a customer problem to production. It's a small team, with no analysts between you and the decision.

The product is public, so you can see what you'd be building before you talk to us: Adapty Flow Builder

What You’ll Do

  • Take features from a customer problem to production: decide with product and design what to build, defend the call, ship it, and check what changed after release.

  • Own the architecture of the editor and move it forward as the product grows: module boundaries, the shape of the document model, where reusable components live, and keeping the editor fast when a flow grows from four screens to hundreds of branches.

  • Ship across the editor surface: canvas and layers, element inspector, selectable groups and states, navigation, actions, variables, and conditional logic.

  • Own the layer that translates the editor config into what the SDKs execute on device. It's a contract with five runtimes, and you'll negotiate it with the mobile team.

  • Close the gap between browser preview and device rendering across layout, typography, media, dark mode, screen sizes, and orientations.

  • Build the document model underneath all of it: nested configs, undo and redo, autosave, drafts versus published versions, and concurrent editing.

  • Build the product around the AI Editor so a generated screen is as inspectable and reversible as a hand-built one: prompt history, per-prompt undo, and a clear view of what changed.

About You

  • 5+ years shipping production web applications in React and TypeScript.

  • You've built editor-class interfaces: canvas, drag and drop, node or graph editors, WYSIWYG, design tools, page builders. Something with a document underneath, not forms over a database.

  • You think in product terms. You can say what problem your last feature solved, who had it, and what changed after you shipped it.

  • You've owned architecture on a product that kept growing. You can explain the boundaries you drew, and what you'd draw differently now.

  • You're at home in complex client state: normalized models, immutability, undo and redo, optimistic updates, versioning.

  • You can own rendering and performance end to end: box model, flex, absolute positioning, reproducing a target exactly rather than approximately, and profiling before you optimize.

  • You go after requirements and contracts yourself, and you say it out loud when something is wrong.

What's in it for you

  • Strong product with industry-best metrics. Adapty is among the top 5% fastest-growing SaaS companies.

  • Exceptional compensation directly tied to your results.

  • Direct communication and ownership. No bureaucracy, no politics, just impact.

  • Flexible remote work. Join us from anywhere or work onsite in our Belgrade or London offices.

  • Professional support. Language learning, sports, health insurance, laptop coverage, and more.

📈 Who We Are:

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair.

Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity.

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale.

In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

The Role:

We're hiring a Senior Product Manager, Rosso.

This is the second product manager on Rosso, reporting into the Rosso Product Lead. Rosso is deeply technical, built on ML-led models and complex engineering covering forecasting, pricing optimisation and portfolio balancing, so this is a role for a technically-minded PM who's happiest closest to the hardest problems. You'll work on complex, important problems as they arise across the Rosso product surface, alongside the other PM on the team, rather than owning one fixed patch. We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

🏅 The Role:

Rosso is tem's core IP, the transaction infrastructure that prices electricity for thousands of businesses, balances portfolios in real time, and sits on the critical path for every deal tem closes. Machine learning is at the heart of Rosso, combining forecasting, optimisation and classical ML to process billions of data points and drive thousands of automated decisions a day. Every inference shapes the prices our customers see, so you can immediately see the impact of your work.

We have proved the concept with MVPs and POCs to grow to 2% of the UK market. Now we want to take it to the next level and build towards a state of the art solution, to fuel our expansion in the UK and take Rosso international.

We're looking for a Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer to lead pricing ML within Rosso, building a platform that proactively drives growth by targeting the right customers to sign at the right time. Your primary focus will be the pricing engine, which sets the fees added to every quote tem serves, carefully balancing growth and margin. You will also contribute to the systems which manage both short and long-term imbalance decisions to determine how tem deals with it’s exposure across its portfolio.

This is a hands-on, senior individual contributor role with significant technical leadership and organisation-wide influence. You will work closely with other MLEs, software engineers and MLOps to bring models to production, and carry real ownership of the technical direction and accountable for its performance.

The right person is energised by the greenfield environment: comfortable taking on ambiguity and able to make progress before the path is fully defined. They have built pricing systems that worked and have learned from the times it hasn't. They'll bring that hard-won judgment to a system where the foundations are still being laid, and where early decisions compound. Success will be turning our current reactive system into a pricing engine which proactively drives growth by targeting the right customers to sign at the right time.

🚀 Responsibilities:

  • Own the technical direction for pricing ML: Define what to build and how within the pricing engine, setting the strategy and roadmap for pricing machine learning as a core piece of tem's IP.

  • Build ML systems for price optimisation: Design and implement models that dynamically set prices, balancing the trade-off between signing probability, portfolio balance and margin maximisation.

  • Solve imbalance problems: Develop probabilistic models to optimise risk management and short-term balancing decisions in a highly dynamic environment.

  • Bridge modelling and production: Own the modelling and data layer while working closely with software engineers and MLOps to ensure models are architected for production, contributing to system design decisions that affect performance and reliability.

  • Communicate pricing decisions clearly: Articulate model behaviour, assumptions, and trade-offs to other technical stakeholders so that pricing decisions are understood across the teams that depend on them.

🎯 Requirements:

Must-haves:

  • Deep experience building ML systems for pricing, revenue optimisation, or decision-making under uncertainty, with a track record of models that went from concept to production and delivered measurable commercial impact.

  • Strong foundation in stochastic optimisation and probabilistic modelling, with the judgement to formulate ambiguous business problems as the right mathematical approach rather than reaching for familiar tools.

  • Proven first-principles reasoning: you choose between stochastic programming, classical ML, reinforcement learning, or a simple heuristic based on the problem, not the technique you know best.

  • The engineering craft to match your modelling depth: production-grade Python, a high bar for code quality and system design, and the ability to work alongside software engineers as a technical peer across the full ML lifecycle.

  • Senior technical leadership in ML: a track record of setting direction for a significant technical area, influencing cross-functional teams, and translating complex model decisions into clear terms for commercial, product, and engineering stakeholders so they are understood and acted on.

Bonus points:

  • Experience with reinforcement learning or causal inference in applied, commercial settings.

  • Familiarity with energy markets, power trading, or portfolio management.

  • PhD or equivalent research depth in a quantitative discipline (statistics, applied mathematics, physics, operations research, or similar).

  • Ability to reason about the trade-offs between optimisation solvers (Gurobi etc) and gradient-based ML methods (PyTorch etc), and the judgement to know when to reach for each.

  • Experience working with high data throughput systems in production.

The mission

At Lucis, we believe healthcare should be preventive, not reactive. We’re building the OS for human longevity to help people add more healthy years to their lives. You can read more about who we are and how we work here.

About you

You thrive in fast‑moving environments, learn by doing, and value feedback as a way to continuously improve. You're curious about AI and how it can be used to move faster and think bigger.

  • 1 to 3+ years in a challenging / fast-growing environment (Series A/B preferred) or a rigorous professional services environment (law, finance, or consulting).

  • You've only worked in large, well-established companies.

  • You need perfect information before making decisions.

How we work

We work together from our Paris hub. We’re passionate about what we’re building and believe the fastest way to create something exceptional is side by side.

 

  • Rigor without ego: Audits, science, and code all deserve the same high bar.

  • Radical ownership: Feedback loops are short; everyone contributes to building the best version of Lucis.

  • Velocity over perfection: We ship daily and prefer a good decision today over a perfect one next week.

 

At Lucis, AI isn't just our product, it's our engine. 100% of our teams are equipped with the best AI agents. You have carte blanche to explore and automate everything that can be, so you can focus exclusively on high-value work.

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
📈 Who We Are:

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair.

Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity.

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale.

In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

The Role

We're hiring a Senior Data Engineer.

Data sits at the core of what tem does. Our time-series data is the spine that runs from pricing through to billing: every transaction depends on it working. You'll be working across a genuinely varied set of workloads: textual data, time-series data, and event streams, each with its own ingestion and reliability challenges, including TSDS.

You'll join our Data Service team of 4, owning the design, reliability, and recovery strategy of specific ingestion pipelines and systems end-to-end. This is an individual contributor role: no team to manage, full ownership of the work you do. The team has more work than hands right now, and this role exists to close that gap so the business can move faster on the data it depends on.

You'll also work closely with our AI initiatives as they grow: the platform you own increasingly becomes the foundation those efforts depend on.

You will:

  • Own the design, reliability, and recovery strategy for the ingestion pipelines and systems in your domain.

  • Maintain and improve the data platform, including working through the existing tech debt backlog.

  • Build monitoring and alerting so issues surface before they become incidents.

  • Set the data quality checks that make an SLA commitment possible, and hold the line on them.

  • Help take the number of data products with a defined SLA from 2 to 10.

Responsibilities

Data Ingestion

  • Own the design, reliability, and resilience of ingestion pipelines end-to-end, including TSDS, with a clear recovery strategy when things break.

  • Build and maintain ETL/ELT pipelines for new and existing data sources.

  • Decide the right approach (batch vs. streaming) for each pipeline in your domain, including high-scale, low-latency requirements for time-series data.

  • Set data quality checks that make an SLA commitment possible, and hold the line on them.

Platform Maintenance

  • Own the day-to-day reliability of the data platform: monitoring, testing, and fixing issues before they become firefights.

  • Own code quality and standards for the systems you're responsible for, including CI checks (linting, tests, coverage).

  • Work through the existing tech debt backlog, prioritising fixes that unblock SLA commitments.

  • Optimise pipelines for performance and cost as data volumes grow.

  • Handle the failure modes specific to energy data: late arrivals, reprocessing, backfills.

Monitoring & Alerting

  • Build and improve observability across your systems so problems surface before they cause downstream impact.

  • Set up alerting tied to the SLAs the team is committing to.

  • Investigate and resolve issues within your domain, escalating genuinely cross-system problems.

Supporting Expansion

  • Help scope and prepare the platform for new data sources tied to international expansion.

  • Flag where current architecture won't hold up as scope grows, even if fixing it isn't your call to make alone.

  • Work closely with the AI team as their data needs on the platform grow.

Requirements

Must haves

  • Strong Python skills, with proven experience building and maintaining production data pipelines.

  • Experience owning the design, reliability, and resilience of a data pipeline or system end-to-end, not just writing pipeline code.

  • AWS or GCP experience.

  • Great communication skills, comfortable working directly with stakeholders to scope and agree SLAs, and explaining technical trade-offs to non-technical audiences.

  • Strong team player, comfortable working independently against a backlog and making judgement calls on prioritisation, while fitting into an existing team of 4.

  • Terraform experience.

Bonus points

  • Experience with time-series data at scale.

  • Experience with modern data stack tooling (Airflow, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, ClickHouse).

  • Experience in energy or climate tech.

  • Background in high-growth startups or scale-ups.

  • Genuine interest in how AI tooling and workflows intersect with data engineering.

We're open to someone who doesn't tick every box here, as long as they bring solid AWS or GCP experience and the ability to own their own work end-to-end.

Benefits & Perks

  • Salary aligned to internal benchmarks and reviewed twice a year.

  • Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission.

  • 25 days holiday plus public holidays. Swap public holidays for the ones that matter most to you, and enjoy your birthday off.

  • Remote first and flexible working, with clear core hours and no internal meetings on Friday afternoons.

Home working and wellbeing budgets:

  • Up to GBP1,200 or EUR1,200 per year for your remote setup.

  • Up to GBP150 or EUR150 per month for wellbeing.

Interview Process

We move fast. Most processes take 2 to 3 weeks from first chat to offer. If you need us to adapt anything, let us know.

  • Intro call with Talent, 30 minutes.

  • Behavioural interview, 60 minutes.

  • Skills interview with cross-functional leaders, 60 to 90 minutes, including a practical exercise.

  • Bar Raiser interview with leadership stakeholders, 45 minutes.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. If you’re excited about this role but not sure you meet every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you. Your unique perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for.

Compensation: £82,700 – £93,350 • Offers Equity

  • • £82,700 – £93,350 • Offers Equity

title: AI Native - Lead Architect
description:
Qui sommes-nous?


Construire. Développer. Pérenniser.

Nous sommes un cabinet de conseil technologique mondial avec une approche d'ingénierie axée sur l’IA, déposée en marque, pour accélérer la livraison de produits numériques et révolutionner la modernisation des plateformes. Nous faisons ce qui est juste, et nous le faisons bien. Nous sommes fiers d’être parmi les New Champions du Forum Économique Mondial et une entreprise certifiée B Corp.

· Nous sommes assez petits pour agir localement, assez grands pour livrer globalement (5 continents, 11 bureaux, plus de 500 experts de plus de 50 nationalités)
· Nous sommes solides et résilients (100 % indépendants et sans dette)
· Nous sommes entrepreneurs et experts passionnés : nous investissons dans ce en quoi nous croyons sincèrement et travaillons en intelligence collective
· Nous sommes positifs, courageux, attentionnés, acteurs et engagés pour l’excellence

Gen-e2

Alors que le marché se contente encore largement de livraisons simplement « augmentées par l’IA », nous avons réinventé le cycle de vie du développement logiciel (SDLC) pour le rendre AI First. Notre approche change la donne en matière de productivité et de qualité, grâce à une collaboration étroite entre l’IA générative et nos meilleurs talents :

  • Nous générons désormais 95 % de l’ensemble du produit — code, documentation, Infrastructure as Code (IaC) et même le design, le tout propulsé par GitHub Copilot.

  • Avec Gen-e2™, nous livrons des produits de bout en bout 2 à 3 fois plus vite que les approches traditionnelles, tout en rehaussant le niveau d’excellence en ingénierie.

    Curieux-se d’en découvrir plus? Lisez notre article The AI-first revolution in Tech: How PALO IT cracked the code of AI-enhanced engineering.

Votre rôle

Pour notre filiale PALO IT LABS basée à Paris et entièrement axée sur le développement de notre méthodologie Gen-e2, vous serez amené à utiliser des outils d’IA de pointe pour accélérer les cycles de développement et stimuler l’innovation.

En tant que membre clé de notre équipe, vous dirigerez des initiatives d'ingénierie à fort impact, pilotées par l’IA, de la phase de découverte à la livraison. Vous serez responsable de l’excellence technique, du développement des compétences de l’équipe et du succès client, en veillant à ce que chaque projet soit aligné avec le modèle Gen-e2 speed-to-impact.


En tant qu’AI Native Lead Architect, vos missions principales seront :

Leadership technique & Architecture

  • Définir les périmètres de services et les architectures de référence, en alignement avec les SLOs, les politiques de sécurité et les objectifs d’optimisation des coûts.

  • Piloter le contexte engineering (fonctionnel et technique) au sein du référentiel produit, en garantissant transparence et qualité via des templates PR automatisés et le respect des normes documentaires.

  • Réaliser des analyses de risques et menaces, en arbitrant entre performances, confidentialité, durabilité et sécurité.

  • Concevoir et mettre en place des garde-fous dans les pipelines CI/CD (ex. anonymisation des données sensibles, vérification des licences, gates de conformité) pour garantir une qualité de niveau entreprise.

  • Améliorer continuellement les indicateurs clés liés à l’efficacité énergétique, aux coûts cloud et à l’accessibilité des systèmes.
     

Engagement collaboratif

  • Faciliter la collaboration avec les sponsors techniques et les équipes produit, en tant que référent d’expertise technique.

  • Participer aux phases de pitch, proof-of-concept et développement de l’écosystème et des artefacts. 
     

Coaching & Facilitation du changement

  • Mentorer et guider les équipes de développement, favorisant une culture d'apprentissage et d'amélioration continue au sein de l'organisation tout en garantissant le delivery du développement technique.

  • Participer aux revues de code, en fournissant des retours constructifs et des suggestions d'amélioration.

  • Rester informé(e) des tendances du secteur, des technologies émergentes et des meilleures pratiques, et évaluer leur impact potentiel sur les opérations commerciales et la performance de l’équipe.

Vous êtes au bon endroit si

  • Vous êtes un(e) architecte logiciel et Tech Lead confirmé(e), reconnu(e) pour votre capacité à intégrer les méthodes IA-First dans des solutions techniques robustes et scalables.

  • Vous avez au moins 6 ans d’expérience en architecture et développement logiciel (Java, .net, Python, React, Angular...) et IA, avec une appétence forte pour la technique et une capacité à être hands-on;

  • Une forte expertise dans la conception et le scaling d’applications cloud-native ou d’architectures AI-First;

  • Une maîtrise approfondie des processus CI/CD, des plateformes cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure), des technologies de containerisation, et des pratiques DevSecOps;

  • Une familiarité avec les approches UX-as-Code et la pensée design system;

  • Une capacité à accompagner et mentorer des équipes diverses dans le développement et l’implémentation de solutions techniques;

  • Un anglais fluide et d’excellentes capacités de communication auprès d’audiences techniques comme non techniques.

  • Vous comprenez des principes de prompt engineering pour une interaction optimale des outils d’IA ;

  • Vous avez une connaissance et curiosité élevées des technologies IA/ML, incluant OpenAI API, LangChain, Hugging Face et le context engineering.

  • Vous avez une pensée critique et analytique pour valider et vérifier le code et les solutions générés par l’IA ;

  • Vous avez une volonté permanente d’apprendre et de vous tenir informé de l’évolution rapide du paysage de l’IA ;

  • Vous êtes sensible aux questions sociales, environnementales et Tech For Good et les intégrez dans ce que vous construisez ;

Les profils de nos consultantes et consultants sont tous diversifiés, et nous sommes fier.es de cette richesse. N’hésitez pas à nous contacter si votre profil ne répond pas à 100 % à cette annonce, nous valorisons également:

  • Le partage de votre engagement, vos connaissances techniques, votre volonté et votre enthousiasme dans des conférences ou communautés de développement et de Software Craftsmanship ;

  • Votre participation à un ou plusieurs projets Open Source, en tant que contributeur.rice, par exemple ;

  • Votre passion pour l'éco-conception, les défis sociaux modernes, l’innovation dans les domaines humains et le développement durable ;

  • Votre engagement dans des associations ou meetups autour de l’humain et de l’environnement.

Ce que nous vous offrons

  • Un terrain de jeu à la hauteur de votre expertise: des missions sélectionnées pour leur complexité, leur exigence d’ingénierie et leur impact business et sociétal.

  • Un coach de carrière dédié qui vous accompagne avec des séances régulières pour structurer, suivre et accélérer vos objectifs de développement.

  • Une communauté technique exigeante et bienveillante: revues de code, pair programming, partage et mentoring pour élever en continu le craft et la rigueur.

  • Parcours de montée en compétences Gen-e2 dès la semaine 1 et tout au long de votre onboarding.

  • Des certifications Microsoft et GitHub financées dès l’onboarding.

  • De l’idée au partage: lab R&D interne, open source by default, conférences tech et dojos d’innovation pour expérimenter, coder, transmettre.

Mais également

  • 🌍 Carrière globale, missions multi-secteurs et potentiellement multi-pays, passerelles entre 11 bureaux.

  • 🏠 Remote Friendly en fonction du projet, les jours en présentiel se vivent chez les clients ou dans nos bureaux à République, Paris avec des réunions d'équipe pour partager et innover. Des missions en full présentiel pourront être déployées. 

  • 🌱 Impact Academy formations climat, numérique responsable et accessibilité intégrées à nos pratiques.

  • 🤝 Engagement solidaire volontariats en équipe, mécénat de compétences.

  • 🥗🩺 Swile pour les tickets resto, Alan pour une santé bien couverte.

Chez PALO IT, la diversité est source d'innovation et d'impact. En tant que B Corp, nous offrons l'égalité des chances et évaluons les candidats uniquement sur leurs compétences, leur potentiel et leur motivation. Nous accueillons les candidatures sans distinction d'identité ou d'expression de genre, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, d'origine, d'ethnie, de religion, de handicap ou de tout autre attribut protégé.

title: Senior AI Engineer, Location AI
description:
Mapbox is the leading real-time location platform for a new generation of location-aware businesses. Mapbox is the only platform that equips organizations with the full set of tools to power the navigation of people, packages, and vehicles everywhere. More than 4 million registered developers have chosen Mapbox because of the platform’s flexibility, security and privacy compliance. Organizations use Mapbox applications, data, SDKs and APIs to create customized and immersive experiences that delight their customers. 

What you'll do

This role is scoped by skill rather than by product. The problems below span multiple departments and show up across our Search and Places data work, our Location and Navigation Intelligence work, and the Platform work that makes Mapbox usable by agents. You'll be hired into one specific team or product area, but you'll work across teams where your expertise meets the highest-priority AI problems. You should expect to move between teams and tech stacks as the work demands.

At this level you own the technical design and delivery of a multi-component AI system, and you are accountable for the quality of what ships in your area.

In this role, you will:

  • Define how the products you own should work, build a measurement framework for it, and build evaluation systems for non-deterministic behavior. Formulate hypotheses around the products we build and seek the signal needed to validate them. Define what a correct result is for a given input and state, determine whether to assemble datasets from real usage or hand-written cases, and gate changes on regression results.

  • Run continuous evaluation of the products we build, whether APIs, SDKs, data representations, or reference applications, from the position of the end user, whether developer, agent, or consumer. Assess the gaps such as misuse of parameters or integration anti-patterns, recommend the fixes, and make sure they land.

  • Own the MVP against an agreed north star technical design, and balance technical perfection against shipping useful increments.

  • Build data pipelines and the tooling around them: ingestion, conflation, entity resolution, quality checks, and the batch and streaming jobs that keep a large dataset current.

  • Track and pull external datasets, models, and benchmarks from published research and open-source releases. Evaluate what fits the problem and constraints , and decide when to adopt what exists versus build your own.

  • Design feedback loops so that using a product generates data that improves it. Instrument systems so failures arrive with enough context to reproduce, then turn the recurring ones into evaluation cases.

  • Design the boundary between a model and the tools it calls. Build or improve the model harness, decide what the model handles, what it delegates, and how to keep it working from the state it actually fetched.

  • Work to a latency and cost target per request: streaming, partial results, caching, model routing, prompt structure.

  • Build the internal harnesses and tools (CLI, MCP, and others) your team needs to iterate quickly, and share the parts that generalize with other teams.

  • Raise the bar on your team through code and design review, and bring other engineers up on eval practice.

  • Some of the technical questions in this area are still open. You will help answer them.

  • Participate in an on-call rotation to ensure our systems remain available to customers 24/7. Team members alternate as the on-call primary responder, which may require immediate response outside normal working hours, including weekends.

What We Believe are Important Traits for This Role

  • Bachelors degree in STEM discipline and 5+ years of software engineering experience, with production ownership of services, pipelines, or SDKs.

  • 2+ years shipping LLM-backed features to real users, in systems that carried error budgets, on-call rotations, and customers who noticed regressions.

  • Direct experience or deep understanding of designing evaluations for non-deterministic systems. You can describe a dataset you built and the failure it caught.

  • Data engineering depth: SQL, at least one distributed processing framework, and experience with pipelines where a wrong record mattered more than a slow one.

  • Fluency with tool calling and agent orchestration, including the failure modes: stale context, hallucinated arguments, silent partial success, unbounded loops.

  • Working knowledge of more than one agent harness, and opinions about where each of them is weak.

  • Strong Python or TypeScript, and comfort reading code in whatever language the caller happens to be written in.

  • Experience diagnosing latency in a distributed request path.

  • Comfort with ambiguity, and the judgment to ship something narrow that works while the general solution is still unclear.

  • Clear written communication. Mapbox is distributed across time zones and we make most decisions in documents and Slack.

Nice to have traits for this role

  • Geospatial data experience: routing, geocoding, POI or address data, OpenStreetMap, or conflation of overlapping sources.

  • Public API or SDK design experience, particularly for developers you never talk to.

  • Experience building against MCP or similar tool transports.

  • Experience running evals in CI, with a commercial harness or one you built.

  • Automotive, in-vehicle infotainment, CarPlay, or Android Auto experience.

  • Voice pipeline experience: streaming ASR, TTS, barge-in, endpointing, wake word.

  • Work under constrained compute, offline, or intermittent connectivity.

  • Experience operating a product through its first external integrations, where the customer finds the gaps before you do.

What We Value

In addition to our core values, which are not unique to this position and are necessary for Mapbox leaders:

  • We value high-performing creative individuals who dig into problems and opportunities.

  • We believe in individuals being their whole selves at work. We commit to this through supportive health care, parental leave, flexibility for the things that come up in life, and innovating on how we think about supporting our people.

  • We emphasize an environment of teaching and learning to equip employees with the tools needed to be successful in their function and the company.

  • We strongly believe in the value of growing a diverse team and encourage people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, abilities, and sexual orientations to apply.

 

How we support you

  • Hybrid/Remote Options: Enjoy flexibility to work comfortably from home or periodically from an office where applicable.

  • Country-Specific Care & Coverage: Private health, dental, and income protection plans tailored to elevate your regional statutory benefits.

  • Family-First Support: Family care, maternity and paternity leave policies to support your growing family.

  • Lifestyle Spending Account: Contributions to support your health, wellness, and personal growth

  • Balance & Brainpower: Mental health support for you and your dependents.

  • Rest & Recharge: Paid time away, company holidays, and generous absence policies.

  • Time Off to Give Back: Dedicated paid volunteering time in addition to your standard PTO.

We are committed to a fair and equitable hiring process. We do not discriminate against any protected class.

title: Sales Director
description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($60M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

The Opportunity

This is one of the highest-leverage commercial roles in the business. As Sales Director, you'll own the entire sales system at Relay — strategy, structure, process, and performance across all four of our segments: Pitstop/Field Sales, Enterprise, Large Parcel, and SME Parcel. You'll set the standards that let each segment lead build well, and you'll be personally accountable for the sum of the results.

Beyond the day-to-day, this role has a genuine builder's brief: creating the infrastructure and team capabilities that take Relay international over the next few years. If you want to shape how a fast-growing carrier goes to market at scale — and leave a lasting mark on how that machine works — this is the role.

What You'll Own

Sales strategy and structure

  • Design the shape of Relay's sales organisation across all four segments — how they relate, where they overlap, how resource is prioritised

  • Define the sales motion for each segment: who it sells to, how, and through which channel

  • Keep strategy current as the business and market evolve

Data and performance management

  • Set the metrics that matter across pipeline, conversion, quota attainment, and productivity

  • Build or oversee the dashboards that surface them

  • Use data to make decisions on resourcing, territory design, and where to invest or pull back — instinct complements data here, it doesn't replace it

Process, structure, and scalability

  • Own the sales playbook, forecasting cadence, deal review process, CRM hygiene standards, and comp and quota-setting principles

  • Upskill and coach the existing team on pitch, process, and performance

  • Build infrastructure that scales for the next three years, not just today's headcount

Team leadership and org design

  • Lead the four segment sales leads (Pitstop/Field, Enterprise, Large Parcel, SME Parcel) and any central sales ops or enablement partners

  • Decide what's centralised across functions versus what each segment lead owns locally

  • Hire, develop, and coach those leads so each can build out their patch well

Global and remote team leadership

  • Lead teams remotely across time zones and geographies as Relay expands into the Americas and Europe

  • Proven capability to do this is a requirement — it can't be learned on the job here

Exec partnership and GTM planning

  • Partner with the CCO and other function leads on revenue planning, headcount decisions, and commercial trade-offs

  • Translate company strategy into a sequenced sales roadmap and GTM direction

  • Push back clearly when targets or timelines aren't realistic

Who Will Thrive in This Role

  • Multi-motion sales leader. You've led more than one kind of sales motion — for example, high-volume SMB or transactional sales alongside enterprise or mid-market relationship-led sales. You're comfortable setting standards and managing performance across both. You've carried a number yourself and led others doing the same. This isn't a role for a single-lane specialist.

  • Data-driven and structured operator. You define the metrics that matter, build or oversee the dashboards, and use data to make resourcing and process calls — not gut feel alone. You have a track record of introducing or significantly upgrading forecasting discipline, CRM hygiene, territory design, and comp structures in ways that improved consistency and scalability. You think in systems across a multi-year horizon, not just the next quarter.

  • Global and remote team builder. You've led sales teams across multiple geographies or time zones, ideally including the US and Europe. You're comfortable setting standards, culture, and expectations remotely. Having helped take a company into a new country is a bonus; the core requirement is proven capability.

  • People leader and org designer. You've led sales managers or leaders — not just individual contributors — and operated at least one layer removed from the front line. You have a track record of hiring and developing leaders beneath you, and making clear calls about what to centralise versus what to delegate.

  • Exec partner. You've partnered directly with a CEO, founder, or C-suite on revenue planning and commercial trade-offs. You can push back on unrealistic targets while maintaining trust, and you can translate company strategy into an actionable, sequenced sales roadmap.

  • Builder, not just operator. You've introduced new process, data infrastructure, or org structure in a previous role — not only operated within a system someone else built. This role is not about being a super-IC closer or a sector-pedigree hire; logistics experience is welcome but not a requirement or a filter.

Compensation, Benefits & Workplace

  • Generous equity, richer than 99% of European startups, with annual top-ups to share Relay’s success.

  • Private health & dental coverage, so comprehensive you’d need to be a partner at a Magic Circle law firm to match it.

  • 25 days of holidays

  • Enhanced parental leave.

  • Hardware of your choice.

  • Extensive perks (gym subsidies, cycle-to-work, Friday office lunch, covered Uber home and dinner for late nights, and more).

Who Thrives at Relay?

LLM-backed features fail probabilistically. Agents take actions no runbook anticipated. "Is my app healthy?" is becoming an unanswerable question for a whole generation of AI-native software. You will build reliability for this kind of software.

Our stack is AI (Codex, Claude, use what you like best), Vue.js, TypeScript, Node.js, Golang, Postgres, ClickHouse and AWS. We ship to prod all day, every day. We practice Agile (not scrum) and take pride in good documentation and good looking products.

We’re a remote-first startup that keeps things simple—low on meetings, high on productivity, and always shipping. If you love building cool things, working async, actually listening to and working with customers, and keeping it lean, you’ll fit right in!

What you'll do

Build and ship with AI

You will actively use coding agents for full stack development, from exploring solutions and generating scaffolding to refactoring, test generation and debugging. At Checkly we push the limits of AI tools every day.

Talk to our users

You will talk directly to the developers, DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams who are on-call, debugging incidents, or wiring Checkly into production pipelines. You will understand their workflows, pain points, and feedback. You use those conversations to validate ideas, course-correct early, and iterate on what you build. Customer calls and the weekly support rotation are part of the job, not a distraction from it.

Find the right problems to solve

In a world where the cost of building software trends to zero, the hard part is picking what to build. You will focus on real developer pain: flaky tests and flaky checks, unclear failures, noisy alerts. You will favour pragmatic solutions that ship quickly, validate assumptions in production, and compound into long-term reliability improvements.

Own your work end to end

From shaping the initial idea, through implementation and rollout, to watching how it behaves in production. You will take part in on-call and help support customers when things don’t work as expected.

What you should have

  • You have shipped features with AI, not just experimented with them. You have taken work from zero to shipped with a comparable stack, made implementation decisions that held up, and put things in front of real users.

  • You have built and run production software. You know the realities of operating software that people depend on: edge cases, incidents, regressions, and the need for observability and follow-up. You are not surprised when things break. You help fix them.

  • You can hold a product conversation, not just a technical one. You can look at a customer problem and reason about whether the thing we are about to build actually solves it.

  • You work well without an office around you. You are autonomous and self-motivated in a remote setup, and you still enjoy getting to know your colleagues and helping other people get unstuck.

  • FULLY remote role, within the UTC-3 to UTC+3 time zones. You need to be able to travel to (other) European countries without having to wait for a visa appointment, for our annual kickoff, a team meetup or a conference.

What you will hate about us

We would rather tell you now than have you find out in month two.

  • We use AI for everything, and we mean everything. AI skepticism is not a thing here. If you have the slightest hesitation about working with AI every day, this is not the place for you, and that is completely fine.

  • We write more than we talk. We are async-first, so a lot of decisions happen in documents and threads, not meetings. If you do your best thinking out loud in a room full of people, you will miss it here.

  • We are lean, so you own the unglamorous parts too. There is no separate QA team, no ops layer to hand things off to, and you are on the support rotation and the on-call rotation like everyone else.

  • We ship constantly and change our minds. Priorities move as we learn from customers. If you need long, stable planning cycles, this will feel chaotic.

  • Customer signals come first, and most of the time they matter more than your instinct. We build what customers actually want, not the clever thing we dreamed up.

Benefits

  • Transparent salary because your salary shouldn't be dictated by how good a negotiator you are. (more info below)

  • Remote-first, flexible work hours, async-first (low meeting, high productivity) and transparent culture

  • Become part of a fast-growing, international, and remote team where your work matters, and your impact won't get lost in layers of bureaucracy.

  • Stock options

  • 27 days of paid vacation + your local public holidays

  • Paid sick leave & up to 14 weeks of paid parental leave

  • Co-working budget or home office setup

  • Annual company kickoffs

  • Employee & contractor options

Find out more here.

What we pay

Fair, competitive, and transparent pay is very important for us. Therefore we work with a standardized salary calculator that includes several factors such as seniority level as well as location.

Apply

Women, non-binary people and POC will seek to match a much higher percentage of requirements before applying. If you're not sure you're the right fit, apply anyway and let us know what you bring to the table. We'd love to hear from you!

We're all about being transparent and setting clear expectations. That's why we've put together our hiring playbook and open-sourced our employee handbook. There you'll find a sneak peek of who we are, how we work and what you can expect in our hiring process.

description:
Location: Fully Remote (Global)

Classification: Full-time; 40 hours per week

Pay Range: €51,000-90,000

Experience: 2+ years as a QA engineer

Welcome to Miaplaza!

Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive homeschool curriculum platform where all students can be successful! Our K-8 platforms include Miacademy, Always Icecream, and Clever Dragons, and our 9-12 options include MiaPrep and MiaPrep Online High School. Our student base is rapidly growing, and we’re hiring for multiple positions across several departments! Our expansion stems from our commitment to providing exceptional educational content and our pursuit of new opportunities. 🚀

▶️ You can hear our CEO, Johannes Ziegler, discuss our company’s values and future!

How you’ll make an impact (position summary):

Miaplaza is dedicated to making education engaging and accessible through innovative online learning platforms. We develop personalized learning experiences for students, helping them grow in a supportive and interactive environment. Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive education curriculum platform where all students can be successful!

The Role

We're looking for a QA Engineer to join our current QA team. You'll take ownership of how we test, validate, and sign off on quality across our platform. We're actively investing in our QA practice: expanding automated test coverage, improving our release testing process, and moving toward a model where quality is embedded throughout the development lifecycle.

You'll report to a technical Engineering Manager and work alongside engineers who value clear test documentation, reliable automation, and confident code releases.

As a mature company, we have legacy systems and established manual testing workflows, but we are transitioning to modern automated testing practices using Playwright and TypeScript. The split between manual and automated work varies, but you should be comfortable working across both, bringing automation where it adds the most value while pragmatically maintaining manual coverage where it's still the right tool.

A core goal of our QA evolution is to make testing faster, more reliable, and less dependent on last-minute changes before each release: replacing fragile manual regression cycles with stable automated suites, reducing flakiness, and building coverage that the whole team can rely on. Every testing investment is measured by whether it improves quality and reduces the team's burden at release time.

What You'll Do

  • Write and maintain automated regression tests; review automation MRs from peers

  • Execute manual testing across web UIs (functional, regression, cross-platform, responsive layouts on mobile/tablet)

  • Create and maintain test cases, checklists, and test documentation in TestRail

  • File clear, actionable bug reports with reproduction steps; collaborate with developers to triage and resolve

  • Own the release testing process to ensure only high-quality changes ship

  • Partner with PMs and designers on requirements review, edge cases, and acceptance criteria

  • Contribute to QA process improvements as we scale (currently a 2-person team growing to 4)

How We Work

We believe you should know what your days look like before you accept an offer.

We don't have much bureaucracy. Small team, direct communication, short decision loops. If you've worked at places where opening a Jira ticket to request a Jira ticket was normal, this isn't that. Here's the reality:

Meetings (yes, we keep them minimal):

  • Daily standup with your product team. Show up, share updates and unblock each other..

  • Sprint planning and retrospectives with your product team, once per sprint.

  • 1:1 with your Engineering Manager - Regular cadence, your agenda.

  • Monthly Engineering all-hands.

  • That's it. The rest of your time is yours to work.

Deployments:

  • Bi-monthly release cadence with a schedule published in advance. As a QA Engineer, you own the release testing window. Coordinating with developers, running regression suites, and signing off on quality before the release.

  • Infrequent ad-hoc hotfixes

Communication:

  • Async-friendly. Documentation-first.

  • Slack/ Jira/ GitLab MRs/ Notion

  • Google Workspace for email and documents.

  • Zoom for video calls.

Timezone:

  • We need significant overlap with typical CET (Central European Time) working hours to coordinate and collaborate synchronously. Additionally we have stakeholders and developers in US timezones that we occasionally need to meet.


What We're Looking For

Requirements (Requisite Skills): 

  • 2+ years of QA engineering experience, including web UI testing

  • 2+ years of experience with Playwright or a similar test automation framework (e.g. Cypress, Selenium, Puppeteer)

  • 2+ years of experience using TypeScript

  • Strong test design skills: comfortable writing and maintaining test cases, checklists, and test documentation

  • Familiarity with QA's role in the SDLC and how to collaborate with developers and PMs

  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail

  • Upper-intermediate English (B2+) for written and spoken communication

  • Strong experience in manual testing and writing manual test cases

Nice to have:

  • Experience with accessibility and/or security testing

How you’ll work with other teams:

Career Growth

We have a defined career ladder. Whether your path leads toward Senior/Staff QA Engineer or Engineering Management, there's room to grow - and we'll work with you to get there.

Onboarding

Every team member gets full support throughout onboarding, and no one expects you to figure out the ins and outs on your own. We'll pair with you, answer every question, and make sure you have the context you need. New hires typically feel very supported at Miaplaza.

What success looks like here: In the first couple of months, you're asking a lot of clarifying questions, reading documentation, exploring the product independently, and writing and running tests with confidence. By months 3-4, you're taking ownership of a specific area, building out test coverage, identifying gaps, and driving quality improvements. By month 5-6, you're contributing meaningfully to the testing strategy for migration and modernisation work and operating independently. The common thread: curiosity, initiative, and the habit of investigating before you ask, but always asking when you need to.

Interview Process

Our process is staged and designed to respect your time. Expect a mix of introductory conversation, technical discussion, and practical evaluation. We want to understand how you think about real problems and testing practices. As part of the process, we will ask for professional references and conduct a background check in accordance with applicable law. If you need any accommodations during the interview process, let us know, we're happy to help.

Compensation

Competitive compensation, open to negotiation based on your experience and expertise. We'll discuss specifics early in the process so neither side wastes time. Since we’re remote-first, every arrangement is different; we tailor time off, benefits, and perks as part of your individual contract to ensure the overall package works for both sides.

Ready to apply?

Join our team at Miaplaza! Start by submitting your application and resume. Our hiring process involves a screening call, followed by a behavioral interview, and two technical interviews.

title: SRE Manager
description:
About Us

Parity is one of the world's most experienced core blockchain infrastructure companies, having built and pioneered some of the most advanced technologies in the blockchain sector. Parity was founded by Dr. Gavin Wood, co-founder and former CTO of Ethereum, the primary engineer behind the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM), inventor of the Solidity programming language, and primary author of the Ethereum Yellowpaper.

People in Our Collective Are

  • Highly motivated to contribute to Parity’s mission and be part of something bigger

  • Excited to work on projects that are groundbreaking and complex

  • Autonomous workers that self-initiate, but also collaborate well with others

  • Taking maximum accountability and having minimum ego at work

  • Comfortable with chaos and adapting to the ever-changing Web3 space

  • Continuously educating themselves about Parity and the wider ecosystem

About the Team

The SRE team is responsible for the infrastructure that makes the Polkadot platform and technology work: test and production network environments, deployment pipelines, observability, and the systems that developers, node operators, and end-user applications across the ecosystem rely on. This spans the full stack from runtime and parachain development environments through to infrastructure supporting live applications and events.

We run environments at different stability tiers, from fast-moving test networks with daily automated updates to production networks with 24/7 on-call coverage. It's a small team, so the role carries broad scope.

The Role

We're looking for an engineering manager who can lead a team of experienced SRE engineers and raise the standard of what reliability looks like in a blockchain infrastructure context.

The team is technically capable. What it needs is someone who can set engineering direction, build the conditions for good work, and think clearly about reliability as a discipline: SLOs, error budgets, blameless postmortems.

What We're Looking For

Systems thinking. You have a genuine understanding of distributed systems and large-scale infrastructure. You don't need to be the most senior engineer technically, but you need to be credible to people who are.

Reliability. You've worked in or led a team that takes SRE seriously. You know what error budgets are actually for, when SLOs are miscalibrated, and how to run postmortems that improve things.

Automation. You get uncomfortable when skilled engineers spend time on work a machine could do. You've built teams that automate away the repetitive work rather than just absorbing it.

People development. You have a track record of engineers growing under your leadership, ideally some of them moving on to bigger things.

Comfort with unusual territory. Blockchain infrastructure has properties that don't map cleanly onto standard cloud operations. You don't need prior Web3 experience, but you shouldn't be put off by it either.

Working at Parity

Remote-first, with offices in Berlin, Lisbon, and London. Parity is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome diversity in our global team and care about everyone in our collective feeling included and welcome.

View our Applicant Notice to see how we use your data.

  • Violaine Yziquel, our CCO, is the hiring manager

What Success Looks Like in This Role

You’ll be at the frontline of our Customer Success motion - helping define it while actively delivering results. We don’t yet have all the tooling, playbooks, or workflows in place - you’ll help build them, while making sure our biggest customers are supported, engaged, and growing.

Success means:

  • Renewals are a no-brainer because value is clear and relationships are deep

  • Expansions happen regularly because opportunities are spotted and acted on

  • Customers lean on us as strategic partners - not just vendors.

Your Three Core Responsibilities

Drive Retention and Expansion Across Strategic Accounts

  • Own a portfolio of high-potential, high-complexity enterprise accounts

  • Drive the full renewal cycle

  • Multithread across stakeholders to ensure broad, embedded relationships

  • Surface commercial opportunities through value-based conversations

Build the Foundations of Customer Success at Fyxer AI

  • Develop scalable, repeatable playbooks for success, renewal, and expansion

  • Help shape our tooling and GTM tech stack - helping choose, implement, and evolve the right systems to support success at scale

  • Define and refine KPIs and dashboards that help us track what matters most for our customers

Be a Strategic Partner to Product, Sales, and Leadership

  • Translate customer insights into product feedback and roadmap influence

  • Collaborate closely with Sales on account planning and pre-to-post handoffs

  • Bring a commercial lens to everything - always thinking about how success drives revenue

What Our Ideal Candidate Looks Like

  • 8+ years in Customer Success or Account Management, with a clear track record of owning revenue (renewals + expansion)

  • Commercially driven - you’re not afraid to talk numbers, push for value, and ask for the upsell

This culture is intense; it requires focus and discipline. So we’ll do everything we can to remove distraction, support your wellbeing, and reward your impact
